The sounds of joy, "the voices of the bride and bridegroom", are also taken away in Jeremiah: in 7:34 the LORD says "I will remove from the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem the sounds of joy and gladness and the voices of the bride and bridegroom", and in 25:10 "I will banish from them the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of the bride and bridegroom, the sound of the millstones, and the light of the lamp"; Revelation 18:22-23 says the sound of a millstone, the light of a lamp and the voices of a bride and bridegroom will never be heard or seen "in you again".
rows.different: Jeremiah 51:63 has a stone tied to "this scroll" and cast "into the Euphrates"; Revelation 18:21 has "a mighty angel" cast "a stone the size of a great millstone" "into the sea". In Isaiah 47 the one addressed says "I will be queen forever" and is told "loss of children, and widowhood" will overtake her "in a single day"; in Revelation 18:7 she says "I sit as queen" and her plagues come "in one day" as "death and grief and famine"; and where Psalms 137:8 and Jeremiah 50:29 repay her as she has done, Revelation 18:6 adds "pay her back double".

rows.title: The prostitute who sits on many waters

Ezekiel: your remnant will be consumed by fire
They will treat you with hatred
Isaiah: sell herself to all the kingdoms on the face of the earth
Jeremiah & the Twelve: You who dwell by many waters
though you dress yourself in scarlet, though you adorn yourself with gold jewelry
the harlot, the seductive mistress of sorcery
Elsewhere: she must be burned in the fire
the dogs will devour the flesh of Jezebel
Revelation: the great prostitute, who sits on many waters
The kings of the earth were immoral with her
dressed in purple and scarlet, and adorned with gold
They will leave her desolate and naked, and they will eat her flesh and burn her with fire
The kings of the earth were immoral with her

rows.alike: Revelation's prostitute "sits on many waters" and Jeremiah 51:13 addresses one "who dwell by many waters"; she is "dressed in purple and scarlet, and adorned with gold" as Jeremiah 4:30 says "dress yourself in scarlet" and "adorn yourself with gold jewelry". Those who "hate" her leave her "naked" and "burn her with fire", as Ezekiel 23 has "They will treat you with hatred", "leave you naked and bare" and "consumed by fire".
rows.different: In Revelation 17:16 it is "the ten horns and the beast" who hate her and "eat her flesh"; in Ezekiel 16:39 it is "your lovers" who leave her naked, and in 2 Kings 9:36 "the dogs" devour "the flesh of Jezebel". Isaiah 23:17 names Tyre, who will "sell herself to all the kingdoms", and Nahum 3:4 a "mistress of sorcery" who "betrays nations"; Revelation has "The kings of the earth" immoral with her and adds "a golden cup full of abominations".

rows.title: Kings, merchants and sailors lament the great city

Ezekiel: Then they will lament for you
They will weep over you with anguish of soul and bitter mourning
gold, the finest of all spices, and precious stones
They exchanged slaves and bronze utensils
The sailors and all the captains of the sea will stand on the shore
You enriched the kings of the earth with your abundant wealth
Isaiah: whose merchants are renowned on the earth
Revelation: the kings of the earth who committed sexual immorality and lived in luxury with her will weep and wail
In fear of her torment, they will stand at a distance
the merchants of the earth will weep and mourn over her
cargo of gold, silver, precious stones, and pearls; of fine linen, purple, silk, and scarlet
of bodies and souls of slaves
Every shipmaster, passenger, and sailor, and all who make their living from the sea, will stand at a distance
What city was ever like this great city?
all who had ships on the sea were enriched by her wealth
your merchants were the great ones of the earth

rows.alike: In both, kings, merchants and seafarers mourn a city: Ezekiel's "sailors and all the captains of the sea will stand on the shore" and Revelation's "Every shipmaster, passenger, and sailor" "will stand at a distance"; Ezekiel's lament asks "Who was ever like Tyre" and Revelation's "What city was ever like this great city?" Both list the city's trade in gold, silver, precious stones, purple, fine linen and slaves, and Isaiah 23:8 calls Tyre's merchants "renowned on the earth" as Revelation 18:23 calls hers "the great ones of the earth".
rows.different: Ezekiel names "Tyre" and her trading partners; Revelation names "the mighty city of Babylon", and its mourners watch "the smoke rising from the fire that consumes her" and say "in a single hour your judgment has come". Ezekiel's mourners "shave their heads" and "wrap themselves in sackcloth", Revelation's "throw dust on their heads"; in Ezekiel 27:33 she "enriched the kings of the earth", in Revelation 18:19 "all who had ships on the sea were enriched".

rows.title: A bride adorned for her husband

Isaiah: as a bride adorns herself with her jewels
as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride
Revelation: His bride has made herself ready
She was given clothing of fine linen, bright and pure
prepared as a bride adorned for her husband

rows.alike: Isaiah 61:10 speaks of a speaker clothed "with garments of salvation" and "a robe of righteousness" and compares this to "a bride" who "adorns herself with her jewels"; Revelation has a bride who "has made herself ready" and the city "prepared as a bride adorned for her husband". Both speak of clothing: Isaiah's "garments of salvation" and "a robe of righteousness", Revelation's "clothing of fine linen, bright and pure".
rows.different: In Isaiah the bride is a comparison ("as a bride") for the speaker whom God "has clothed", and 62:5 says "your God will rejoice over you" as a bridegroom over his bride; Revelation names "the marriage of the Lamb" and "the holy city, the new Jerusalem". Revelation 19:8 says "She was given clothing of fine linen, bright and pure" and "the fine linen she wears is the righteous acts of the saints".

rows.title: The great supper: birds gorged on flesh

Ezekiel: Call out to every kind of bird and to every beast of the field
a great feast on the mountains of Israel
you will eat fat until you are gorged and drink blood until you are drunk
eat your fill of horses and riders, of mighty men and warriors of every kind
Revelation: cried out in a loud voice to all the birds flying overhead
gather together for the great supper of God
eat the flesh of kings and commanders and mighty men, of horses and riders
all the birds gorged themselves on their flesh

rows.alike: Both summon birds to a meal, Ezekiel's "great feast" and Revelation's "great supper of God", to eat "horses and riders" and "mighty men", and both use the word "gorged".
rows.different: Ezekiel calls "every beast of the field" as well as birds, names a "sacrificial feast" "on the mountains of Israel", and adds "drink blood until you are drunk"; Revelation calls "all the birds" through "an angel standing in the sun", adds "kings and commanders" and "everyone slave and free, small and great", and reports that "all the birds gorged themselves on their flesh".

rows.title: No place found for them

Daniel: The wind carried them away, and not a trace of them could be found
Revelation: Earth and heaven fled from His presence, and no place was found for them

rows.alike: In both, what was there can no longer be found: Daniel's "not a trace of them could be found" and Revelation's "no place was found for them".
rows.different: In Daniel it is "the iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold" of the statue, which "became like chaff" and were carried off by "The wind", and "the stone" then "filled the whole earth"; in Revelation it is "Earth and heaven", which "fled from His presence" before "a great white throne".

rows.title: The holy city: on a high mountain, foursquare, its gates, foundations and light

Ezekiel: set me on a very high mountain, on whose southern slope was a structure that resembled a city
the gates of the city will be named after the tribes of Israel
4,500 cubits on the north side, 4,500 cubits on the south side, 4,500 cubits on the east side, and 4,500 cubits on the west side
Isaiah: all your walls of precious stones
No longer will the sun be your light by day
the LORD will be your everlasting light
they will never be shut, day or night
the wealth of the nations will come to you
the uncircumcised and unclean will no longer enter you
Gospels & letters: built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets
Elsewhere: a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst
each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes
twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high
engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes
Revelation: a mountain great and high, and showed me the holy city
twelve gates inscribed with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel
twelve foundations bearing the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb
The city lies foursquare, with its width the same as its length
12,000 stadia in length and width and height
the eleventh jacinth, and the twelfth amethyst
the city has no need of sun or moon to shine on it
Its gates will never be shut
into the city will be brought the glory and honor of the nations
nothing unclean will ever enter it

rows.alike: Ezekiel is set "on a very high mountain" and John on "a mountain great and high" to see a city whose gates bear the names of "the tribes of Israel", measured the same on every side; Isaiah's city, like Revelation's, has gates that "will never be shut", needs no "sun" for its light, has foundations of "sapphires", receives the wealth of "the nations", and is not entered by the "unclean".
rows.different: Ezekiel's city measures "4,500 cubits" on each of four sides and 1 Kings 6:20's inner sanctuary "twenty cubits" each way, where Revelation's city is "12,000 stadia in length and width and height"; Revelation's foundations bear "the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb", while Ephesians 2:20 has "the foundation of the apostles and prophets" and Exodus 28:21 and 39:14 set the names of the twelve tribes on stones, "engraved like a seal". Isaiah 60:19 says "the LORD will be your everlasting light"; Revelation 21:23 says "the glory of God illuminates the city, and the Lamb is its lamp".

rows.title: A new name

Isaiah: You will be called by a new name that the mouth of the LORD will bestow
to His servants He will give another name
Revelation: a white stone inscribed with a new name

rows.alike: Both speak of a new name given: Isaiah's "a new name that the mouth of the LORD will bestow" and "another name" for "His servants", Revelation's "a white stone inscribed with a new name" for "the one who overcomes".
rows.different: Revelation 2:17 puts the name on "a white stone", "known only to the one who receives it", and 3:12 writes on the overcomer "the name of My God", "the name of the city of My God" and "My new name"; Isaiah 62:2 adds "Nations will see your righteousness", and 65:15 sets the servants' "another name" against "your name as a curse".

rows.title: The abomination of desolation

Daniel: set up the abomination of desolation
the abomination of desolation set up
Gospels & letters: spoken of by the prophet Daniel
the abomination of desolation standing where it should not be

rows.alike: Daniel 11:31 and 12:11, Matthew 24:15 and Mark 13:14 all use the words "the abomination of desolation", and Daniel 9:27 has "the abomination that causes desolation"; Matthew names it as "spoken of by the prophet Daniel".
rows.different: Daniel sets it beside the ending of sacrifice ("abolish the daily sacrifice", "the daily sacrifice is abolished"), places it "on the wing of the temple" in 9:27, and counts "1,290 days" in 12:11; Matthew has it "standing in the holy place" and Mark "standing where it should not be", and both add "let the reader understand", with Mark going on "let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains".

rows.title: Heaven is My throne, earth My footstool

Isaiah: Heaven is My throne, and earth is My footstool
What kind of house will you build for Me?
Gospels & letters: by heaven, for it is God's throne
or by the earth, for it is His footstool
Heaven is My throne and the earth is My footstool
What kind of house will you build for Me, says the Lord
Elsewhere: build for Me a house to dwell in

rows.alike: All three call heaven a throne and the earth a footstool: Isaiah has "Heaven is My throne, and earth is My footstool", and Matthew has "by heaven, for it is God's throne" and "by the earth, for it is His footstool". Isaiah and Acts both go on to ask "What kind of house will you build for Me?", and 2 Samuel 7:5 has "Are you the one to build for Me a house to dwell in?"
rows.different: Isaiah and Acts speak in the first person ("My throne", "My footstool"), while Matthew speaks of "God's throne" and "His footstool" in a command "not to swear at all" and adds "or by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King". Isaiah opens "This is what the LORD says", where Acts places "says the Lord" inside the question.

rows.title: Their worm will never die, their fire never quenched

Isaiah: their worm will never die, their fire will never be quenched
Gospels & letters: their worm never dies, and the fire is never quenched

rows.alike: Both speak of a worm that does not die and a fire that is not quenched: "their worm will never die" (Isaiah) and "their worm never dies" (Mark).
rows.different: Isaiah has "their fire will never be quenched" and Mark "the fire is never quenched". Isaiah sets the words beside "the corpses of the men who have rebelled against Me" who "will be a horror to all mankind"; Mark introduces them with "where".

rows.title: The messenger who prepares the way

Isaiah: Prepare the way for the LORD in the wilderness
make a straight highway for our God in the desert
prepare the way, take every obstacle out of the way of My people
prepare the way for the people
Jeremiah & the Twelve: I will send My messenger, who will prepare the way before Me
Gospels & letters: A voice of one calling in the wilderness
Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him
I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You
I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way
Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him
go on before the Lord to prepare the way for Him
Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him
I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You
Elsewhere: prepare the way for His steps
Revelation: prepare the way for the kings of the East

rows.alike: Each has a way prepared: "Prepare the way for the LORD" (Isaiah, and "Prepare the way for the Lord" in Matthew, Mark and Luke 3:4), and a sent messenger "who will prepare the way" (Malachi; "who will prepare Your way" in Matthew, Mark and Luke 7:27). Luke 1:76 says a child "will go on before the Lord to prepare the way for Him".
rows.different: Isaiah has "Prepare the way for the LORD in the wilderness" and "make a straight highway for our God in the desert", where Matthew and Mark have "A voice of one calling in the wilderness" and "make straight paths for Him". Malachi's messenger prepares the way "before Me"; in Matthew and Mark the messenger is sent "ahead of You" to prepare "Your way".

rows.title: Elijah sent before the day

Jeremiah & the Twelve: I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and awesome Day of the LORD
he will turn the hearts of the fathers to their children
Gospels & letters: he is the Elijah who was to come
Elijah does indeed come, and he will restore all things
in the spirit and power of Elijah
to turn the hearts of the fathers to their children

rows.alike: Each speaks of Elijah coming: "I will send you Elijah the prophet" (Malachi), "the Elijah who was to come" (Matthew 11:14), "Elijah does indeed come" (Matthew 17:11). Malachi and Luke share the words "turn the hearts of the fathers to their children".
rows.different: Malachi continues "and the hearts of the children to their fathers", where Luke continues "and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous". Malachi names "Elijah the prophet" coming "before the coming of the great and awesome Day of the LORD"; Luke has "in the spirit and power of Elijah", and Matthew 17:11 adds "he will restore all things".

rows.title: New heavens and a new earth

The Prophets: I will create new heavens and a new earth
the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, will endure before Me
The letters: we are looking forward to a new heaven and a new earth, where righteousness dwells
Revelation: Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth
the first heaven and earth had passed away, and the sea was no more

rows.alike: Isaiah 65:17 and 66:22 speak of "new heavens and a new earth" and "the new heavens and the new earth"; 2 Peter 3:13 and Revelation 21:1 both have "a new heaven and a new earth".
rows.different: Isaiah has "heavens" and God speaking ("I will create", "which I will make, will endure before Me"); 2 Peter has "we are looking forward to" and adds "where righteousness dwells"; Revelation has "I saw" and adds "the first heaven and earth had passed away, and the sea was no more".

rows.title: Heaven and earth wear out and pass away

The Prophets: the heavens will vanish like smoke, the earth will wear out like a garment
they will all wear out like a garment
The skies will be rolled up like a scroll
Psalms & elsewhere: In the beginning You laid the foundations of the earth
They will perish, but You remain; they will all wear out like a garment. Like clothing You will change them
Gospels & Acts: Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away
Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away
Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away
until heaven and earth pass away
it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away
The letters: They will perish, but You remain; they will all wear out like a garment
You will roll them up like a robe
The heavens will disappear with a roar
Revelation: Earth and heaven fled from His presence, and no place was found for them
the first heaven and earth had passed away
The sky receded like a scroll being rolled up

rows.alike: Isaiah 51:6 says "the earth will wear out like a garment", and Psalm 102:26 and Hebrews 1:11 say "they will all wear out like a garment"; Hebrews 1:11 has the same words as the first part of Psalm 102:26. Matthew 24:35 says "Heaven and earth will pass away" and Revelation 21:1 that "the first heaven and earth had passed away". Mark 13:31 and Luke 21:33 have Matthew 24:35's words. Isaiah 34:4 says "The skies will be rolled up like a scroll" and Revelation 6:14 "The sky receded like a scroll being rolled up".
rows.different: What remains differs: "My salvation will last forever" (Isaiah 51:6), "but You remain" (Psalm 102:26; Hebrews 1:11), "My words will never pass away" (Matthew 24:35); Psalm 102:27 goes on "But You remain the same, and Your years will never end". Hebrews 1:12 has "You will roll them up like a robe", which Psalm 102:26 does not, and "like a garment they will be changed" where Psalm 102:26 has "Like clothing You will change them"; 2 Peter 3:10 has "The heavens will disappear with a roar", Revelation 20:11 "Earth and heaven fled from His presence", and Revelation 21:1 "had passed away". Matthew 5:18 and Luke 16:17 speak of the Law: "until heaven and earth pass away", "easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for a single stroke of a pen to drop out of the Law".

rows.title: The former things passed away; all things new

The Prophets: Do not call to mind the former things
Behold, I am about to do something new
The former things will not be remembered
Behold, the former things have happened, and now I declare new things
proclaim to us the former things
I foretold the former things long ago
Gospels & Acts: in the renewal of all things
The letters: The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!
Revelation: the former things have passed away
Behold, I make all things new

rows.alike: Isaiah 42:9, 43:19, 2 Corinthians 5:17 and Revelation 21:5 each say "Behold" before something new: "I declare new things", "I am about to do something new", "the new has come", "I make all things new". Isaiah 42:9, 43:18, 65:17 and Revelation 21:4 speak of "the former things", and 2 Corinthians 5:17 and Revelation 21:4 both say what is old or former "has passed away" or "have passed away".
rows.different: Isaiah says "Do not call to mind the former things" and that they "will not be remembered"; Revelation 21:4 says they "have passed away". Isaiah has "I am about to do", Revelation "I make", and 2 Corinthians "the new has come", said of "anyone" who "is in Christ"; Matthew has "the renewal of all things" and Acts "the restoration of all things".

rows.title: Created new: heavens, a heart, a person

The Prophets: I will create new heavens and a new earth
I will create Jerusalem to be a joy
Psalms & elsewhere: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me
The letters: if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation
What counts is a new creation
to create in Himself one new man out of the two

rows.alike: Each speaks of creating or of a new creation: "I will create new heavens" (Isaiah 65:17), "I will create Jerusalem to be a joy" (Isaiah 65:18), "Create in me a clean heart" and "renew a right spirit" (Psalm 51:10), "a new creation" (2 Corinthians 5:17; Galatians 6:15), "to create in Himself one new man" (Ephesians 2:15).
rows.different: What is created differs: "new heavens and a new earth" and "Jerusalem" in Isaiah; "a clean heart" in the one praying in Psalm 51; "anyone" who "is in Christ" in 2 Corinthians; "one new man out of the two" in Ephesians. Isaiah speaks as God ("I will create"), the Psalm asks God ("O God"), and Galatians sets "a new creation" against "circumcision nor uncircumcision".

rows.title: Death swallowed up; no more death

The Prophets: He will swallow up death forever
Where, O Death, are your plagues? Where, O Sheol, is your sting?
The letters: Death has been swallowed up in victory
Where, O Death, is your victory? Where, O Death, is your sting?
The last enemy to be destroyed is death
so that our mortality may be swallowed up by life
Revelation: there will be no more death
Then Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire

rows.alike: Isaiah 25:8 says "He will swallow up death forever" and 1 Corinthians 15:54 "Death has been swallowed up in victory"; Hosea 13:14 asks "Where, O Sheol, is your sting?" and 1 Corinthians 15:55 "Where, O Death, is your sting?". Revelation 21:4 says "there will be no more death".
rows.different: 1 Corinthians 15:54 calls its words "the saying that is written"; Hosea pairs "plagues" and "sting" with Death and Sheol, 1 Corinthians "victory" and "sting" with Death. 1 Corinthians 15:26 calls death "The last enemy to be destroyed", Revelation 20:14 has "Death and Hades" "thrown into the lake of fire", and 2 Corinthians 5:4 has "our mortality" "swallowed up by life".

rows.title: Tears wiped away; no more weeping or crying

The Prophets: The Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from every face
The sounds of weeping and crying will no longer be heard in her
Revelation: God will wipe away every tear from their eyes
He will wipe away every tear from their eyes
there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain

rows.alike: Isaiah 25:8 ("The Lord GOD will wipe away the tears") and Revelation 7:17 ("God will wipe away every tear") name who will wipe them away, and Revelation 21:4 says "He will wipe away every tear"; Isaiah 65:19 and Revelation 21:4 both say "crying" will be no more.
rows.different: Isaiah 25:8 has "the tears from every face", Revelation "every tear from their eyes". Isaiah 65:19 says "weeping and crying will no longer be heard in her", of Jerusalem; Revelation 21:4 lists "death or mourning or crying or pain"; Isaiah 35:10 has "sorrow and sighing will flee" as "the redeemed of the LORD will return and enter Zion with singing".

rows.title: God's dwelling with them; they will be His people

The Prophets: My dwelling place will be with them; I will be their God, and they will be My people
I will be their God, and they will be My people
they will become My people. I will dwell among you
I will dwell among the Israelites forever
I will dwell among them forever
Psalms & elsewhere: I will dwell among the Israelites and be their God
I will make My dwelling place among you
I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be My people
I will dwell among the Israelites and will not abandon My people Israel
The letters: I will dwell with them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people
Revelation: the dwelling place of God is with man, and He will dwell with them. They will be His people

rows.alike: Exodus 29:45, Leviticus 26:11, 1 Kings 6:13, Ezekiel 37:27, 43:7 and 43:9, Zechariah 2:11, 2 Corinthians 6:16 and Revelation 21:3 each say God will dwell, or have His dwelling place, among or with a people: "I will dwell among the Israelites" (Exodus 29:45; 1 Kings 6:13), "I will dwell among them forever" (Ezekiel 43:9), "My dwelling place will be with them" (Ezekiel 37:27), "I will dwell with them" (2 Corinthians 6:16), "He will dwell with them" (Revelation 21:3). Leviticus 26:12, Jeremiah 31:33, Ezekiel 37:27, Zechariah 2:11, 2 Corinthians 6:16 and Revelation 21:3 add that they will be His people.
rows.different: Exodus has "among the Israelites", Zechariah 2:11 "many nations will join themselves to the LORD", and Revelation 21:3 "the dwelling place of God is with man"; the earlier passages speak as "I", Revelation as "He". Leviticus 26:12 has "I will walk among you" and 2 Corinthians 6:16 "walk among them"; 2 Corinthians gives the words with "As God has said" and "we are the temple of the living God".

rows.title: I will be his God, and he will be My son

Psalms & elsewhere: I will raise up your descendant after you
I will be his Father, and he will be My son
I will be his Father, and he will be My son
The letters: I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty
Revelation: The one who overcomes will inherit all things, and I will be his God, and he will be My son

rows.alike: All have God saying "I will be" with a son: "he will be My son" (2 Samuel 7:14; 1 Chronicles 17:13; Revelation 21:7) and "you will be My sons and daughters" (2 Corinthians 6:18).
rows.different: 2 Samuel 7:14 has "his Father", said of the descendant God will raise up ("I will raise up your descendant after you", 7:12); 2 Corinthians has "a Father to you" and "sons and daughters"; Revelation 21:7 has "his God", said of "The one who overcomes", who "will inherit all things".

rows.title: The holy city, Jerusalem; nothing unclean will enter

The Prophets: O Jerusalem, holy city! For the uncircumcised and unclean will no longer enter you
The unclean will not travel it
The letters: the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother
you have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem
Revelation: the holy city, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God
the new Jerusalem that comes down out of heaven from My God
But nothing unclean will ever enter it

rows.alike: Isaiah 52:1 calls Jerusalem "holy city" and Revelation 21:2 has "the holy city, the new Jerusalem"; Isaiah 52:1 says the "unclean will no longer enter you" and Revelation 21:27 "nothing unclean will ever enter it". Galatians, Hebrews and Revelation each name a Jerusalem with heaven or what is above: "the Jerusalem above", "the heavenly Jerusalem", "coming down out of heaven".
rows.different: Isaiah 52:1 calls to Zion, "Awake, awake, clothe yourself with strength", and Isaiah 35:8 says "The unclean will not travel" a highway, "the Way of Holiness"; Galatians says "she is our mother", Hebrews "you have come to Mount Zion", and Revelation "I saw" it "coming down out of heaven from God".

rows.title: A bride adorned for her husband

The Prophets: He has clothed me with garments of salvation and wrapped me in a robe of righteousness
as a bride adorns herself with her jewels
as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so your God will rejoice over you
Revelation: the marriage of the Lamb has come, and His bride has made herself ready
She was given clothing of fine linen, bright and pure
prepared as a bride adorned for her husband

rows.alike: Isaiah 61:10 has "a bride adorns herself" and Revelation 21:2 "a bride adorned for her husband"; Isaiah 62:5 has a bridegroom who "rejoices over his bride" and Revelation 19:7 "the marriage of the Lamb". Both speak of clothing: "garments of salvation" and "a robe of righteousness" in Isaiah, "clothing of fine linen, bright and pure" in Revelation.
rows.different: In Isaiah the bride is a comparison ("as a bride") for the speaker whom "He has clothed", and 62:5 says "your God will rejoice over you"; Revelation 21:2 has "the holy city, the new Jerusalem" "prepared as a bride", and 19:8 says "the fine linen she wears is the righteous acts of the saints".

rows.title: Its light, its open gates, and the nations

The Prophets: Nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn
Your gates will always stand open; they will never be shut, day or night
so that the wealth of the nations may be brought into you
No longer will the sun be your light by day
the LORD will be your everlasting light
Revelation: the city has no need of sun or moon to shine on it, because the glory of God illuminates the city, and the Lamb is its lamp
By its light the nations will walk, and into it the kings of the earth will bring their glory
Its gates will never be shut at the end of the day, because there will be no night there
into the city will be brought the glory and honor of the nations
they will have no need for the light of a lamp or of the sun

rows.alike: Isaiah 60 and Revelation 21 both say gates "will never be shut" ("Your gates"; "Its gates"), that nations and kings come to or walk by the light ("Nations will come to your light"; "By its light the nations will walk"), that what the nations have is brought in ("the wealth of the nations may be brought into you"; "into the city will be brought the glory and honor of the nations"), and that the sun is not the light: "No longer will the sun be your light by day"; "the city has no need of sun or moon".
rows.different: Isaiah 60:19 says "the LORD will be your everlasting light", Revelation 21:23 "the glory of God illuminates the city, and the Lamb is its lamp". Isaiah's gates are open "day or night"; Revelation's are not shut "because there will be no night there". Isaiah has "wealth", Revelation "glory and honor".

rows.title: A river flowing out

Genesis: a river flowed out of Eden to water the garden
The Prophets: water flowing from under the threshold of the temple
living water will flow out from Jerusalem
Gospels & Acts: Streams of living water will flow from within him
Revelation: a river of the water of life, as clear as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb

rows.alike: Each has water flowing out: "a river flowed out of Eden", "water flowing from under the threshold of the temple", "living water will flow out from Jerusalem", "Streams of living water will flow from within him", "a river of the water of life ... flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb". Genesis 2:10 and Revelation 22:1 both have "a river".
rows.different: It flows "out of Eden" (Genesis 2:10), "from under the threshold of the temple" (Ezekiel 47:1), "out from Jerusalem" (Zechariah 14:8), "from within him" (John 7:38, "as the Scripture has said"), and "from the throne of God and of the Lamb" (Revelation 22:1). Genesis's river "branched into four headwaters", Zechariah's runs "half of it toward the Eastern Sea and the other half toward the Western Sea", and Revelation's is "as clear as crystal".

rows.title: The tree of life

Genesis: in the middle of the garden were the tree of life
take also from the tree of life, and eat, and live forever
a whirling sword of flame to guard the way to the tree of life
Psalms & elsewhere: She is a tree of life to those who embrace her
The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life
desire fulfilled is a tree of life
A soothing tongue is a tree of life
Revelation: I will grant the right to eat from the tree of life in the Paradise of God
On either side of the river stood a tree of life
Blessed are those who wash their robes, so that they may have the right to the tree of life
God will take away his share in the tree of life and the holy city

rows.alike: Genesis, Proverbs and Revelation all have the words "tree of life". Genesis and Revelation both speak of eating from it: "take also from the tree of life, and eat" (Genesis 3:22), "eat from the tree of life" (Revelation 2:7).
rows.different: In Genesis and Revelation "the tree of life" is a tree with a place: "in the middle of the garden" (Genesis 2:9), "in the Paradise of God" (Revelation 2:7), "On either side of the river" (Revelation 22:2); Genesis 3:24 has "a whirling sword of flame to guard the way to the tree of life", and Revelation speaks of "the right to the tree of life" (22:14). In Proverbs four things are each called "a tree of life": "She" (3:18), "The fruit of the righteous" (11:30), "desire fulfilled" (13:12) and "A soothing tongue" (15:4).

rows.title: Fruit each month and leaves for healing

The Prophets: Along both banks of the river, fruit trees of all kinds will grow
Each month they will bear fruit
Their fruit will be used for food and their leaves for healing
Revelation: On either side of the river stood a tree of life
bearing twelve kinds of fruit and yielding a fresh crop for each month
the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations

rows.alike: Both have fruit-bearing on both sides of a river ("Along both banks of the river"; "On either side of the river"), fruit every month ("Each month they will bear fruit"; "a fresh crop for each month"), and leaves "for healing" or "for the healing of the nations".
rows.different: Ezekiel has "fruit trees of all kinds" whose "leaves will not wither", fed by "the water from the sanctuary"; Revelation has "a tree of life, bearing twelve kinds of fruit", and healing "of the nations".

rows.title: No longer any curse

Genesis: cursed are you above all livestock and every beast of the field
cursed is the ground because of you; through toil you will eat of it all the days of your life
The Prophets: Therefore a curse has consumed the earth, and its inhabitants must bear the guilt
Revelation: No longer will there be any curse

rows.alike: Genesis 3:17 has "cursed is the ground" and Isaiah 24:6 "a curse has consumed the earth"; Revelation 22:3 says "No longer will there be any curse".
rows.different: In Genesis God speaks a curse on the serpent ("cursed are you") and on "the ground because of you", with "toil"; Isaiah 24:6 has "its inhabitants must bear the guilt"; Revelation 22:3 names no one cursed and is followed by "The throne of God and of the Lamb will be within the city".

rows.title: Let the thirsty come and drink

The Prophets: Come, all you who are thirsty, come to the waters
Come, buy wine and milk without money and without cost
Gospels & Acts: If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me and drink
the water I give him will become in him a fount of water springing up to eternal life
Revelation: To the thirsty I will give freely from the spring of the water of life
let the one who is thirsty come, and the one who desires the water of life drink freely

rows.alike: Isaiah 55:1, John 7:37 and Revelation 22:17 each call the "thirsty" to "come"; Isaiah has "without cost" and Revelation "freely".
rows.different: Isaiah says "come to the waters" and "buy wine and milk without money"; John 7:37 says "come to Me and drink"; Revelation has "the water of life" and "the spring of the water of life", John 4:14 "a fount of water springing up to eternal life". In Revelation 22:17 "The Spirit and the bride say" it.

rows.title: They will see His face

Psalms & elsewhere: I will behold Your face in righteousness; when I awake
Even after my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh I will see God
Gospels & Acts: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God
The letters: Now we see but a dim reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face
we will be like Him, for we will see Him as He is
Revelation: They will see His face, and His name will be on their foreheads

rows.alike: Psalm 17:15 has "I will behold Your face", 1 Corinthians 13:12 "face to face" and Revelation 22:4 "They will see His face"; Job 19:26 and Matthew 5:8 both have "will see God".
rows.different: Who sees differs: "I" (Psalm 17:15; Job 19:26), "the pure in heart" (Matthew 5:8), "we" (1 Corinthians; 1 John), "They" (Revelation 22:4). Job has "in my flesh" and "after my skin has been destroyed", the Psalm "when I awake", 1 Corinthians sets it after "Now we see but a dim reflection", 1 John adds "we will be like Him", and Revelation adds "His name will be on their foreheads".

rows.title: A kingdom forever; they will reign

The Prophets: I saw One like the Son of Man coming with the clouds of heaven

the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess it forever

Psalms & elsewhere: I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever
Gospels & Acts: He will reign over the house of Jacob forever. His kingdom will never end!
you who have followed Me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel
The letters: if we endure, we will also reign with Him
He hands over the kingdom to God the Father
He must reign until He has put all His enemies under His feet
Revelation: The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ, and He will reign forever and ever
they will reign forever and ever

rows.alike: 2 Samuel 7:13, Daniel 7:14, Luke 1:33, Revelation 11:15 and Revelation 22:5 each speak of a kingdom or a reign without end: "the throne of his kingdom forever" (2 Samuel 7:13), "will never be destroyed" (Daniel 7:14), "His kingdom will never end" (Luke 1:33), "He will reign forever and ever" (Revelation 11:15), "they will reign forever and ever" (Revelation 22:5).
rows.different: Who reigns differs: "his kingdom" in 2 Samuel, "One like the Son of Man" and "the saints of the Most High" in Daniel, "He" over "the house of Jacob" in Luke, "we will also reign with Him" in 2 Timothy, "our Lord and of His Christ" and then "they" in Revelation; Matthew has "twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel". 1 Corinthians 15:24-25 has "He must reign until" and "He hands over the kingdom to God the Father".

rows.title: The dead will rise, to life or to judgment

The Prophets: Your dead will live; their bodies will rise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust!
many who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake, some to everlasting life, but others to shame and everlasting contempt
Gospels & Acts: all who are in their graves will hear His voice
those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment
there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked
The letters: For the trumpet will sound, the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed
with the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ will be the first to rise
Revelation: I saw the dead, great and small, standing before the throne
the dead were judged according to their deeds

rows.alike: Isaiah 26:19 and Daniel 12:2 both speak of those in "the dust" who "awake"; Daniel 12:2, John 5:29 and Acts 24:15 each name two outcomes or two kinds raised: "some to everlasting life, but others to shame", "the resurrection of life" and "the resurrection of judgment", "both the righteous and the wicked". 1 Corinthians 15:52 and 1 Thessalonians 4:16 both have a trumpet.
rows.different: Daniel has "many" and John "all who are in their graves"; Isaiah has "their bodies will rise", 1 Corinthians "raised imperishable", 1 Thessalonians "the dead in Christ will be the first to rise". Revelation 20:12 has "the dead, great and small, standing before the throne" and "judged according to their deeds".

rows.title: They will shine like the stars and the sun

The Prophets: the wise will shine like the brightness of the heavens
those who lead many to righteousness will shine like the stars forever and ever
Psalms & elsewhere: those who love You shine like the sun at its brightest
Gospels & Acts: the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father

rows.alike: Daniel 12:3 and Matthew 13:43 say people "will shine like" a light of the sky; Judges 5:31 says "may those who love You shine like the sun at its brightest".
rows.different: Daniel has "the wise" and "those who lead many to righteousness", shining "like the brightness of the heavens" and "like the stars forever and ever"; Matthew has "the righteous", shining "like the sun in the kingdom of their Father"; Judges 5:31 has "those who love You" shining "like the sun at its brightest".

rows.title: The first man from the dust; the earthly and the heavenly

Genesis: the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground
the man became a living being
he had a son in his own likeness, after his own image
The letters: The first man Adam became a living being
the last Adam a life-giving spirit
The first man was of the dust of the earth, the second man from heaven
just as we have borne the likeness of the earthly man, so also shall we bear the likeness of the heavenly man

rows.alike: 1 Corinthians 15:45 has "So it is written: The first man Adam became a living being"; Genesis 2:7 has "the man became a living being". Genesis 2:7 has man formed "from the dust of the ground" and 1 Corinthians 15:47 "of the dust of the earth". Genesis 5:3 and 1 Corinthians 15:49 both have "likeness".
rows.different: Genesis 2:7 has God who "breathed the breath of life into his nostrils"; 1 Corinthians 15:45 has "the last Adam a life-giving spirit" and 1 Corinthians 15:47 "the second man from heaven", which Genesis 2:7 does not have. Genesis 5:3 is Adam's son "in his own likeness"; 1 Corinthians 15:49 has "the likeness of the earthly man" and "the likeness of the heavenly man".

rows.title: A new heart and a new spirit

The Prophets: I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you
put a new spirit within them
fashion for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit
Psalms & elsewhere: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me

rows.alike: Both join heart and spirit, and a spirit "within": "a new heart and put a new spirit within you" (Ezekiel 36:26), "a clean heart" and "a right spirit within me" (Psalm 51:10).
rows.different: Ezekiel 36:26 and 11:19 have God giving ("I will give you a new heart"); Ezekiel 18:31 tells Israel to "fashion for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit"; Psalm 51:10 is a prayer, "Create in me". Ezekiel has a "new" heart and spirit, the Psalm a "clean" heart and a "right" spirit.

rows.title: Written on hearts, not on tablets of stone

The Prophets: I will put My law in their minds and inscribe it on their hearts
I will remove your heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh
Psalms & elsewhere: tablets of stone inscribed by the finger of God
The letters: written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts
I will put My laws in their minds and inscribe them on their hearts
I will put My laws in their hearts and inscribe them on their minds

rows.alike: Jeremiah 31:33 and Hebrews 8:10 both have "in their minds" and "on their hearts"; Exodus 24:12 and 31:18 and Deuteronomy 4:13, 5:22 and 9:9 have "tablets of stone", and 2 Corinthians 3:3 "not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts"; Ezekiel 36:26 sets "heart of stone" against "heart of flesh".
rows.different: Exodus 31:18 has "inscribed by the finger of God" and Exodus 24:12 "with the law and commandments I have written"; Deuteronomy 4:13 and 5:22 have "two tablets of stone" and Deuteronomy 9:9 "the tablets of the covenant"; 2 Corinthians has "written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God". Jeremiah has "My law", Hebrews "My laws", and Hebrews 10:16 reverses the order: "in their hearts" and "on their minds".

rows.title: I will pour out My Spirit

The Prophets: I will pour out My Spirit on your descendants
until the Spirit is poured out upon us from on high. Then the desert will be an orchard
And afterward, I will pour out My Spirit on all people
I will put My Spirit within you
I will pour out My Spirit on the house of Israel
I will pour out My Spirit in those days
Psalms & elsewhere: poured out my spirit on you
Gospels & Acts: In the last days, God says, I will pour out My Spirit on all people
I will pour out My Spirit in those days
The letters: the washing of new birth and renewal by the Holy Spirit
This is the Spirit He poured out on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior

rows.alike: Isaiah 44:3, Joel 2:28 and 2:29, Ezekiel 39:29 and Acts 2:17 and 2:18 all have "I will pour out My Spirit"; Isaiah 32:15 has "the Spirit is poured out upon us" and Titus 3:6 "the Spirit He poured out on us".
rows.different: On whom: "your descendants" (Isaiah 44:3), "upon us from on high" (Isaiah 32:15), "all people" (Joel 2:28; Acts 2:17), "the house of Israel" (Ezekiel 39:29), "My menservants and maidservants" (Joel 2:29; Acts 2:18), "on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior" (Titus). Acts 2:17 begins "In the last days, God says"; Joel 2:28 begins "And afterward"; Joel 2:29 and Acts 2:18 have "in those days", and Acts 2:18 adds "and they will prophesy". Titus speaks in the past ("He poured out") and of "renewal by the Holy Spirit"; Ezekiel 36:27 has "put My Spirit within you", and Isaiah 32:15 adds "the desert will be an orchard".

rows.title: The new self, in the image of its Creator

Genesis: God created man in His own image
The letters: to put off your former way of life, your old self
to put on the new self, created to be like God in true righteousness and holiness
have put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge in the image of its Creator

rows.alike: Genesis 1:27 has "created man in His own image" and Colossians 3:10 "in the image of its Creator"; Ephesians 4:24 has "created to be like God". Ephesians and Colossians both speak of putting on "the new self".
rows.different: Genesis tells what God "created", "male and female"; Ephesians tells readers "to put off" the "old self" and "to put on the new self", while Colossians says they "have put on the new self, which is being renewed". Ephesians adds "in true righteousness and holiness", Colossians "in knowledge".

rows.title: The wolf with the lamb; a covenant with the beasts

Genesis: I now establish My covenant with you and your descendants after you
the birds, the livestock, and every beast of the earth
The Prophets: The wolf will live with the lamb
the lion will eat straw like the ox
They will neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mountain
The wolf and the lamb will feed together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox
They will neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mountain
I will make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air and the creatures that crawl on the ground
I will make with them a covenant of peace and rid the land of wild animals
Psalms & elsewhere: you will have a covenant with the stones of the field, and the wild animals will be at peace with you

rows.alike: Isaiah 11 and 65:25 both put the wolf with the lamb (11:6), have "the lion will eat straw like the ox" (11:7), and say "They will neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mountain" (11:9). Hosea 2:18, Job 5:23 and Genesis 9:9-10 each speak of a covenant and the animals: "the beasts of the field and the birds of the air", "the wild animals will be at peace with you", "the birds, the livestock, and every beast of the earth".
rows.different: Isaiah 11:6 has "The wolf will live with the lamb", 65:25 "will feed together". Genesis 9 has God's covenant "with you and your descendants" and with the animals; Hosea's is made "for them with the beasts", Job's is "with the stones of the field", and Ezekiel 34:25's "covenant of peace" will instead "rid the land of wild animals".

rows.title: Dust the serpent's food

Genesis: On your belly will you go, and dust you will eat, all the days of your life
The Prophets: the food of the serpent will be dust
They will lick the dust like a snake

rows.alike: Genesis 3:14 says to the serpent "dust you will eat", and Isaiah 65:25 says "the food of the serpent will be dust".
rows.different: Genesis 3:14 is spoken to the serpent with "cursed are you" and "all the days of your life"; Isaiah 65:25 sets it beside "The wolf and the lamb will feed together"; Micah 7:17 says of others, "They will lick the dust like a snake".

rows.title: Build houses and live in them; plant vineyards and eat

The Prophets: They will build houses and dwell in them; they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit
No longer will they build houses for others to inhabit, nor plant for others to eat
they will rebuild and inhabit the ruined cities. They will plant vineyards and drink their wine
Psalms & elsewhere: You will build a house but will not live in it. You will plant a vineyard but will not enjoy its fruit

rows.alike: All three pair building and dwelling with planting vineyards: "build houses and dwell in them" and "plant vineyards" (Isaiah 65:21), "rebuild and inhabit" and "plant vineyards" (Amos 9:14), "build a house" and "plant a vineyard" (Deuteronomy 28:30).
rows.different: Deuteronomy 28:30 has the reverse: "but will not live in it" and "but will not enjoy its fruit", and Isaiah 65:22 says "No longer will they build houses for others to inhabit". Isaiah has "eat their fruit" and Amos "drink their wine" and "the ruined cities"; Isaiah 65:22 adds "as is the lifetime of a tree, so will be the days of My people".

rows.title: A new covenant; sins remembered no more

The Prophets: I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah
It will not be like the covenant I made with their fathers
I will forgive their iniquities and will remember their sins no more
I will make a covenant of peace with them; it will be an everlasting covenant
Gospels & Acts: This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you
The letters: This cup is the new covenant in My blood
ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit
I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah
I will forgive their iniquities and will remember their sins no more

rows.alike: Jeremiah 31:31 and 34 and Hebrews 8:8 and 12 have the same words: "I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah" and "will remember their sins no more"; Isaiah 43:25 has "remembers your sins no more". Luke 22:20 and 1 Corinthians 11:25 both have "This cup is the new covenant in My blood", and Hebrews 8:13, 9:15 and 12:24 have "a new covenant".
rows.different: Jeremiah sets it against "the covenant I made with their fathers"; Hebrews introduces the words with "God found fault with the people and said". Isaiah 43:25 has "blots out your transgressions for My own sake". Luke adds "which is poured out for you", 1 Corinthians "in remembrance of Me", and 2 Corinthians 3:6 "not of the letter but of the Spirit"; Ezekiel 37:26 has "a covenant of peace" and "an everlasting covenant". Hebrews 8:13 has "He has made the first one obsolete", and Hebrews 9:15 and 12:24 have "mediator of a new covenant".

rows.title: Where righteousness dwells

The Prophets: until the Spirit is poured out upon us from on high
Then justice will inhabit the wilderness, and righteousness will dwell in the fertile field
The work of righteousness will be peace
The letters: a new heaven and a new earth, where righteousness dwells

rows.alike: Isaiah 32:16 says "righteousness will dwell" and 2 Peter 3:13 "where righteousness dwells".
rows.different: Isaiah has righteousness "in the fertile field" and "justice" in "the wilderness", after "the Spirit is poured out upon us from on high" (32:15); 2 Peter has "a new heaven and a new earth".

rows.title: Be ever hearing, but never understanding

The Prophets: Be ever hearing, but never understanding; be ever seeing, but never perceiving
Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn and be healed
Gospels & Acts: You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving
In them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled
Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them
they may be ever seeing but never perceiving, and ever hearing but never understanding; otherwise they might turn and be forgiven
though seeing, they may not see; though hearing, they may not understand
He has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts, so that they cannot see with their eyes, and understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them
You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving
The Holy Spirit was right when He spoke to your fathers through Isaiah the prophet
Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them

rows.alike: Matthew 13:14, Mark 4:12 and Acts 28:26 have Isaiah 6:9's "ever hearing" and "never understanding", "ever seeing" and "never perceiving", and Luke 8:10 has "though seeing" and "though hearing". Matthew 13:15 and Acts 28:27 have Isaiah 6:10's "see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn", and John 12:40 has "see with their eyes, and understand with their hearts, and turn".
rows.different: Isaiah 6:9 has "Go and tell this people" and "Be ever hearing" where Matthew 13:14 and Acts 28:26 have "You will be ever hearing"; Mark 4:12 puts seeing first and ends "turn and be forgiven", Isaiah 6:10 ends "turn and be healed", and Matthew 13:15, John 12:40 and Acts 28:27 end "turn, and I would heal them". Matthew 13:14 says "In them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled", and Acts 28:25 "The Holy Spirit was right when He spoke to your fathers through Isaiah the prophet".

rows.title: Behold, the virgin will be with child

The Prophets: Behold, the virgin will be with child and give birth to a son, and will call Him Immanuel
Gospels & Acts: Behold, the virgin will be with child and will give birth to a son, and they will call Him Immanuel
All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet
She will give birth to a Son
Behold, you will conceive and give birth to a son

rows.alike: Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:23 both have "Behold, the virgin will be with child", "give birth to a son" and "call Him Immanuel"; Matthew 1:21 has "She will give birth to a Son", and Luke 1:31 "Behold, you will conceive and give birth to a son".
rows.different: Isaiah 7:14 has "and will call Him Immanuel" and Matthew 1:23 "and they will call Him Immanuel", and Matthew 1:23 goes on "which means, 'God with us'". Isaiah 7:14 opens "Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign", and Matthew 1:22 introduces the words with "All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet". Matthew 1:21 and Luke 1:31 have "you are to give Him the name Jesus".

rows.title: The people walking in darkness have seen a great light

The Prophets: the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali
the Way of the Sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations
The people walking in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of the shadow of death, a light has dawned
Elsewhere in the Old Testament: in darkness and in the shadow of death
out of darkness and the shadow of death
Gospels & Acts: Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the Way of the Sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles
the people living in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of the shadow of death, a light has dawned
to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah
those who live in darkness and in the shadow of death

rows.alike: Isaiah 9:1-2 and Matthew 4:15-16 both have "Zebulun", "Naphtali", "the Way of the Sea, beyond the Jordan", and "have seen a great light; on those living in the land of the shadow of death, a light has dawned"; Luke 1:79 has "those who live in darkness and in the shadow of death", and Psalm 107:10 and 14 have "darkness and the shadow of death".
rows.different: Isaiah 9:1 has "Galilee of the nations" and Isaiah 9:2 "The people walking in darkness"; Matthew 4:15-16 has "Galilee of the Gentiles" and "the people living in darkness", without Isaiah's "In the past He humbled" and "in the future He will honor". Matthew 4:14 introduces the words with "to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah". Luke 1:79 goes on "to guide our feet into the path of peace", and Psalm 107:14 "broke away their chains".

rows.title: Prepare the way for the LORD

The Prophets: Prepare the way for the LORD in the wilderness; make a straight highway for our God in the desert
Every valley shall be lifted up, and every mountain and hill made low
the glory of the LORD will be revealed, and all humanity together will see it
prepare the way, take every obstacle out of the way of My people
prepare the way for the people
who will prepare the way before Me
Elsewhere in the Old Testament: to prepare the way for His steps
Gospels & Acts: A voice of one calling in the wilderness
Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him
This is he who was spoken of through the prophet Isaiah
A voice of one calling in the wilderness
Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him
As it is written in Isaiah the prophet
A voice of one calling in the wilderness
Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him
as it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet
Every valley shall be filled in, and every mountain and hill made low
And all humanity will see God's salvation
I am a voice of one calling in the wilderness
Make straight the way for the Lord
John replied in the words of Isaiah the prophet
to prepare the way for Him
Revelation: to prepare the way for the kings of the East

rows.alike: All four Gospels have "voice of one calling" with "in the wilderness", and Matthew 3:3, Mark 1:3 and Luke 3:4 have "Prepare the way for the Lord", as Isaiah 40:3 has "Prepare the way for the LORD"; Malachi 3:1 has "who will prepare the way before Me", Luke 1:76 "to prepare the way for Him" and Psalm 85:13 "to prepare the way for His steps"; Luke 3:5 has "every mountain and hill made low", as Isaiah 40:4 does.
rows.different: Isaiah 40:3 has "Prepare the way for the LORD in the wilderness" and "make a straight highway for our God in the desert"; Matthew 3:3, Mark 1:3 and Luke 3:4 have "A voice of one calling in the wilderness" and "make straight paths for Him", and John 1:23 has "I am a voice of one calling in the wilderness" and "Make straight the way for the Lord". Luke 3:5-6 has "filled in" where Isaiah 40:4 has "lifted up", and "all humanity will see God's salvation" where Isaiah 40:5 has "the glory of the LORD will be revealed, and all humanity together will see it"; Matthew 3:3 says "This is he who was spoken of through the prophet Isaiah".

rows.title: See, I lay a stone in Zion

The Prophets: See, I lay a stone in Zion, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone
the one who believes will never be shaken
a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense
The letters: See, I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense; and the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame
Anyone who believes in Him will never be put to shame
It is just as the Scripture says
See, I lay in Zion a stone, a chosen and precious cornerstone; and the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame
A stone of stumbling and a rock of offense

rows.alike: Romans 9:33 and 1 Peter 2:6 have "See, I lay in Zion" and "the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame"; Romans 9:33 and 1 Peter 2:8 have Isaiah 8:14's "stone of stumbling and a rock of offense".
rows.different: Isaiah 28:16 has "See, I lay a stone in Zion", "a tested stone, a precious cornerstone" and "the one who believes will never be shaken"; Romans 9:33, 10:11 and 1 Peter 2:6 have "believes in Him will never be put to shame", and 1 Peter 2:6 has "a chosen and precious cornerstone". Romans 9:33 has "a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense", which Isaiah 28:16 does not have and Isaiah 8:14 does. The words are introduced with "as it is written" (Romans 9:33), "It is just as the Scripture says" (Romans 10:11) and "For it stands in Scripture" (1 Peter 2:6).

rows.title: Honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me

The Prophets: These people draw near to Me with their mouths and honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me. Their worship of Me is but rules taught by men
Elsewhere in the Old Testament: You are ever on their lips, but far from their hearts
Gospels & Acts: These people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me
They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men
These people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me
Isaiah prophesied correctly about you hypocrites, as it is written
They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men

rows.alike: Matthew 15:8 and Mark 7:6 have "These people" and "honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me", as Isaiah 29:13 does; Jeremiah 12:2 has "on their lips, but far from their hearts".
rows.different: Isaiah 29:13 also has "draw near to Me with their mouths", which Matthew and Mark do not have, and ends "Their worship of Me is but rules taught by men" where they have "They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men". In both Gospels the words follow "Isaiah prophesied correctly about you". Jeremiah 12:2 has "You are ever on their lips", where Isaiah 29:13, Matthew and Mark have "honor Me with their lips".

rows.title: He will swallow up death forever

The Prophets: He will swallow up death forever
The Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from every face
The letters: Death has been swallowed up in victory
then the saying that is written will come to pass
Revelation: God will wipe away every tear from their eyes
He will wipe away every tear from their eyes
there will be no more death

rows.alike: 1 Corinthians 15:54 has death "swallowed up", as Isaiah 25:8 has "He will swallow up death forever"; Revelation 7:17 and 21:4 have "wipe away every tear", as Isaiah 25:8 has "wipe away the tears from every face".
rows.different: 1 Corinthians 15:54 has "Death has been swallowed up in victory" where Isaiah 25:8 has "forever", and calls it "the saying that is written". Isaiah has "the tears from every face" and Revelation "every tear from their eyes"; Revelation 21:4 goes on "there will be no more death".

rows.title: Who has believed our message?

The Prophets: Who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed?
Gospels & Acts: Lord, who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?
This was to fulfill the word of Isaiah the prophet
The letters: Lord, who has believed our message?

rows.alike: John 12:38 and Romans 10:16 have "who has believed our message?", and John 12:38 also has "And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?"
rows.different: John 12:38 and Romans 10:16 open with "Lord, who has believed", where Isaiah 53:1 has no "Lord," before the question; Romans 10:16 has only the first question. John 12:38 says "This was to fulfill the word of Isaiah the prophet", and Romans 10:16 "For Isaiah says".

rows.title: Surely He took up our infirmities

The Prophets: Surely He took up our infirmities and carried our sorrows
Gospels & Acts: He took up our infirmities and carried our diseases
This was to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah

rows.alike: Both have "took up our infirmities and carried our".
rows.different: Isaiah 53:4 has "Surely" and "carried our sorrows", and goes on "yet we considered Him stricken"; Matthew 8:17 has "carried our diseases" and introduces the words with "This was to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah".

rows.title: He was led like a lamb to the slaughter

The Prophets: He was led like a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is silent, so He did not open His mouth
By oppression and judgment He was taken away, and who can recount His descendants? For He was cut off from the land of the living
Gospels & Acts: He was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and as a lamb before the shearer is silent, so He did not open His mouth
In His humiliation He was deprived of justice. Who can recount His descendants? For His life was removed from the earth
who is the prophet talking about, himself or someone else?

rows.alike: Both have "led like a", "to the slaughter", "is silent, so He did not open His mouth" and "recount His descendants".
rows.different: Isaiah 53:7 has "like a lamb" and "a sheep before her shearers", Acts 8:32 "like a sheep" and "a lamb before the shearer"; Isaiah 53:8 has "By oppression and judgment He was taken away" and "cut off from the land of the living", Acts 8:33 "In His humiliation He was deprived of justice" and "His life was removed from the earth". The eunuch, "reading Isaiah the prophet", asks "who is the prophet talking about, himself or someone else?"

rows.title: My house will be called a house of prayer

The Prophets: for My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations
Gospels & Acts: My house will be called a house of prayer
My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations
My house will be a house of prayer

rows.alike: All three Gospels have "My house" and "a house of prayer", and Mark 11:17 has the whole of "My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations", as Isaiah 56:7 does.
rows.different: Matthew 21:13 and Luke 19:46 do not have "for all the nations", and Luke 19:46 has "will be" where Isaiah 56:7 has "will be called". In each Gospel the words follow "It is written" or "Is it not written" and are followed by "a den of robbers".

rows.title: A den of robbers

The Prophets: Has this house, which bears My Name, become a den of robbers in your sight?

rows.alike: All three Gospels have "a den of robbers", the words of Jeremiah 7:11.
rows.different: Jeremiah 7:11 asks "Has this house, which bears My Name, become a den of robbers in your sight?"; in the Gospels the words are "But you have made it" (Mark 11:17, Luke 19:46) or "But you are making it" (Matthew 21:13) "a den of robbers", after "a house of prayer".

rows.title: The Spirit of the Lord GOD is on Me

The Prophets: The Spirit of the Lord GOD is on Me, because the LORD has anointed Me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent Me
to proclaim liberty to the captives
to proclaim the year of the LORD's favor
Gospels & Acts: The Spirit of the Lord is on Me, because He has anointed Me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent Me to proclaim liberty to the captives
recovery of sight to the blind, to release the oppressed
to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor
the scroll of the prophet Isaiah was handed to Him
Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing

rows.alike: Both have "anointed Me to preach good news to the poor", "He has sent Me", "to proclaim liberty to the captives" and "to proclaim the year of the"; Luke 4:18 has "the oppressed", as Isaiah 58:6 does; Jeremiah 34:8 has "to proclaim liberty".
rows.different: Luke 4:18 has "recovery of sight to the blind" and "to release the oppressed", where Isaiah 61:1 has "to bind up the brokenhearted" and "freedom to the prisoners" and Isaiah 58:6 has "to set the oppressed free"; Luke 4:19 has "the year of the Lord's favor", and Isaiah 61:2 goes on "and the day of our God's vengeance". Luke 4:21 has "Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing".

rows.title: Heaven is My throne, and earth is My footstool

The Prophets: Heaven is My throne, and earth is My footstool. What kind of house will you build for Me? Or where will My place of repose be?
Has not My hand made all these things?
Elsewhere in the Old Testament: build for Me a house to dwell in
Gospels & Acts: Heaven is My throne and the earth is My footstool. What kind of house will you build for Me, says the Lord, or where will My place of repose be?
Has not My hand made all these things?
by heaven, for it is God's throne

rows.different: Proverbs 3:11 says "do not reject" and "do not loathe His rebuke", where Hebrews 12:5 says "do not take lightly" and "do not lose heart when He rebukes you"; Proverbs 3:12 ends "as does a father the son in whom he delights", Hebrews 12:6 "He chastises every son He receives". Job 5:17 and Psalm 94:12 call the man disciplined "Blessed", and in Revelation 3:19 the speaker says it of himself: "Those I love I rebuke and discipline".

rows.title: He gives grace to the humble

The letters & Revelation: James 4:6
God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.
1 Peter 5:5
God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.

The letters & Revelation: James 5:20
cover over a multitude of sins
1 Peter 4:8

rows.title: If your enemy is hungry

The letters & Revelation: Romans 12:20

rows.alike: Both say "If your enemy is hungry" and "if he is thirsty", and both go on "For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head".
rows.different: Proverbs has "give him food to eat" and "give him water to drink", Romans "feed him" and "give him a drink"; Proverbs 25:22 ends "and the LORD will reward you", which Romans 12:20 does not have, and Romans opens "On the contrary".

rows.title: A dog returns to its vomit

The letters & Revelation: 2 Peter 2:22

rows.title: Do not boast about tomorrow

Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.
The letters & Revelation: James 4:13
Today or tomorrow we will go to this or that city
James 4:14
You do not even know what will happen tomorrow!
James 4:16
you boast in your proud intentions. All such boasting is evil.

rows.alike: Both join boasting to "tomorrow" and answer it with what is not known: "you do not know what a day may bring" (Proverbs 27:1), "You do not even know what will happen tomorrow" (James 4:14).

rows.title: He catches the wise in their craftiness

The letters & Revelation: 1 Corinthians 3:19

rows.alike: The same words in both: "He catches the wise in their craftiness".

rows.title: The LORD knows the thoughts of man, that they are futile

Psalms: The LORD knows the thoughts of man, that they are futile.

The letters & Revelation: Romans 11:35

rows.title: Like grass that withers, like a flower of the field

grass on the rooftops, scorched before it is grown

he will pass away like a flower of the field

withers the plant; its flower falls

but the word of the Lord stands forever.

rows.alike: Isaiah 40:6-8 and 1 Peter 1:24-25 share "All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flowers of the field", "the grass withers and the flowers fall" and a word that "stands forever"; Psalm 103:15 and James 1:10 both have "like a flower of the field", and 2 Kings 19:26, Isaiah 37:27 and Psalm 129:6 have "grass on the rooftops".
rows.different: Psalm 103:15 says it of "man", Psalm 102:11 the speaker of himself ("I wither away like grass"), Psalm 92:7 of "the wicked", Isaiah 51:12 of "a son of man" and James 1:10 of "the one who is rich"; Isaiah 40:8 has "the word of our God", 1 Peter 1:25 "the word of the Lord". Isaiah 66:14, "you will flourish like grass", uses the likeness for flourishing.

rows.title: Man is but a breath, a vapor

Job: my life is but a breath
my days are but a breath
Psalms: each man at his best exists as but a breath
surely each man is but a vapor

Job: our days on earth are but a shadow
like a fleeting shadow, he does not endure
Psalms: My days are like lengthening shadows
I am fading away like a lengthening shadow
his days are like a passing shadow
Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: he passes through his fleeting life like a shadow

rows.alike: 1 Chronicles 29:15 "Our days on earth are like a shadow" and Job 8:9 "our days on earth are but a shadow" are almost the same words; Psalm 144:4 has "his days are like a passing shadow" and Psalm 102:11 "My days are like lengthening shadows".
rows.different: 1 Chronicles 29:15 adds "without hope" and begins "we are foreigners and strangers in Your presence"; Job 8:9 begins "we were born yesterday and know nothing"; Ecclesiastes 6:12 asks "who knows what is good for a man", and Ecclesiastes 8:13 says of the wicked that "their days will not lengthen like a shadow".

rows.title: A thousand years like a day

Psalms: in Your sight a thousand years are but a day that passes, or a watch of the night
The letters & Revelation: 2 Peter 3:8
With the Lord a day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years are like a day.

rows.alike: Both set "a thousand years" beside "a day".
rows.different: Psalm 90:4 is spoken to God, "in Your sight", and adds "or a watch of the night"; 2 Peter 3:8 says "With the Lord" and gives it both ways, "a day is like a thousand years" as well.

rows.title: Their voice has gone out into all the earth

Psalms: their voice has gone out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world.
The letters & Revelation: Romans 10:18
Their voice has gone out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world.

rows.alike: The same words in both: "their voice has gone out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world".
rows.different: Psalm 19:4 goes on "In the heavens He has pitched a tent for the sun"; Romans 10:18 gives the words as the answer to "did they not hear? Indeed they did".

rows.title: Whoever would love life and see good days

Psalms: Who is the man who delights in life, who desires to see good days?
Keep your tongue from evil and your lips from deceitful speech.

Turn away from evil and do good
The letters & Revelation: 1 Peter 3:10
Whoever would love life and see good days must keep his tongue from evil and his lips from deceitful speech.
1 Peter 3:11
He must turn from evil and do good; he must seek peace and pursue it.
1 Peter 3:12
For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and His ears are inclined to their prayer. But the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.

rows.alike: Both run in the same order: "see good days", the tongue kept "from evil" and the lips "from deceitful speech", "do good", "seek peace and pursue it", eyes "on the righteous", ears "inclined to their" cry or prayer, and the face "against those who do evil". Psalm 37:27 has "Turn away from evil and do good" as well.
rows.different: Psalm 34:12 asks "Who is the man who delights in life", where 1 Peter 3:10 says "Whoever would love life"; the Psalm's commands ("Keep your tongue", "Turn away") are "must" in 1 Peter; "their cry" in Psalm 34:15 is "their prayer" in 1 Peter 3:12, and Psalm 34:16 goes on "to wipe out all memory of them from the earth", which 1 Peter does not have.

rows.title: Not one of his bones will be broken

Psalms: He protects all his bones; not one of them will be broken.
Elsewhere in the Old Testament: you may not break any of the bones

Gospels & Acts: Not one of His bones will be broken.

rows.alike: Psalm 34:20 has "not one of them will be broken" and John 19:36 "Not one of His bones will be broken"; Exodus 12:46 and Numbers 9:12 forbid breaking "any of the bones" or "any of its bones".
rows.different: Exodus 12:46 and Numbers 9:12 are commands, and Numbers 9:12 is about the Passover ("They must observe the Passover according to all its statutes"); Psalm 34:20 says "He protects all his bones"; John 19:36 brings its words in with "so that the Scripture would be fulfilled".

rows.title: Taste and see that the LORD is good

The letters & Revelation: 1 Peter 2:3

rows.title: He has scattered abroad his gifts to the poor

Psalms: He has scattered abroad his gifts to the poor; his righteousness endures forever
The letters & Revelation: 2 Corinthians 9:9
He has scattered abroad His gifts to the poor; His righteousness endures forever.

rows.alike: Psalm 112:9 and 2 Corinthians 9:9 share "scattered abroad", "gifts to the poor" and "righteousness endures forever"; Psalm 111:3 and Psalm 112:3 have "righteousness endures forever" as well.

rows.title: Make a level path for your feet

Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: Make a level path for your feet
The letters & Revelation: Hebrews 12:13
Make straight paths for your feet

rows.alike: Both say "Make" a path "for your feet".
rows.different: Proverbs 4:26 has "a level path" and goes on "all your ways will be sure"; Hebrews 12:13 has "straight paths" and gives the reason "so that the lame may not be disabled, but rather healed".

rows.title: If the righteous, how much more the ungodly and the sinner

The letters & Revelation: 1 Peter 4:18
If it is hard for the righteous to be saved, what will become of the ungodly and the sinner?

rows.alike: Both open with "If", name "the righteous", and end with "the ungodly and the sinner".
rows.different: Proverbs 11:31 has the righteous who "receive their due on earth" and says "how much more"; 1 Peter 4:18 has "If it is hard for the righteous to be saved" and asks "what will become of" the rest.

rows.title: Better to be told, "Come up here!"

Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: Do not exalt yourself in the presence of the king, and do not stand in the place of great men
it is better to be told, “Come up here!” than to be demoted in the presence of the prince
Gospels & Acts: do not sit in the place of honor
in humiliation, you will have to take the last place
Friend, move up to a better place

rows.alike: Both warn against taking a high place ("the place of great men", "the place of honor") and set being called up ("Come up here!", "Friend, move up to a better place") against being put lower ("demoted", "in humiliation").
rows.different: Proverbs 25:6-7 is set before "the king" and "the prince"; Luke 14:8-10 at "a wedding banquet" with a "host", and Luke 14:10 adds "you will be honored in front of everyone at the table with you".

rows.title: Do not move an ancient boundary stone

Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: Do not move an ancient boundary stone which your fathers have placed.

Elsewhere in the Old Testament: You must not move your neighbor's boundary marker, which was set up by your ancestors

like those who move boundary stones

rows.alike: All speak of moving a boundary stone (in Deuteronomy 19:14, a "boundary marker"); Deuteronomy 19:14 "set up by your ancestors" and Proverbs 22:28 "which your fathers have placed" both name who set it.
rows.different: Deuteronomy 19:14 says "your neighbor's" and 27:17 "his neighbor's", and 27:17 adds "Cursed is he who moves"; Proverbs says "ancient", and 23:10 adds "the fields of the fatherless"; Job 24:2 sets it beside "they pasture stolen flocks"; Hosea 5:10 says it of "The princes of Judah".

rows.title: They will inherit the land

Psalms: his descendants will inherit the land

Elsewhere in the Old Testament: he will enable Israel to inherit the land
