Gospels & Acts: Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.

rows.alike: Each has "inherit the land" or, in Matthew 5:5, "inherit the earth"; Psalm 37:11 "the meek will inherit the land" and Matthew 5:5 "the meek, for they will inherit the earth" both name the meek.
rows.different: They name who inherits: "those who hope in the LORD" (Psalm 37:9), "those He blesses" (37:22), "The righteous" (37:29), "his descendants" (Psalm 25:13), "he who seeks refuge in Me" (Isaiah 57:13); in Deuteronomy 1:38 Joshua will "enable" Israel to inherit it, and in 3:28 "enable them". Matthew 5:5 has "the earth" and opens "Blessed are".

rewarding him according to his righteousness

rewarding him according to his righteousness
repay each man according to all his ways, since You know his heart

I will judge you according to your ways and repay you for all your abominations

Gospels & Acts: He will repay each one according to what he has done
The letters & Revelation: Romans 2:6

2 Timothy 4:14
The Lord will repay him according to his deeds.
Revelation 2:23
I will repay each of you according to your deeds
Revelation 22:12
to give to each one according to what he has done

rows.alike: Psalm 62:12 "You will repay each man according to his deeds", Proverbs 24:12 "repay a man according to his deeds", Romans 2:6 "will repay each one according to his deeds" and Revelation 2:23 "repay each of you according to your deeds" are nearly the same words; 1 Kings 8:39 and 2 Chronicles 6:30 have "repay each man according to all his ways".
rows.different: Some are prayers ("May the LORD repay the evildoer", 2 Samuel 3:39; "Repay them according to their deeds", Psalm 28:4), some questions ("Will He not repay", Proverbs 24:12), and in 2 Samuel 22:21, Psalm 18:20, 2 Samuel 22:25 and Psalm 18:24 the speaker says of himself "He has repaid me according to the cleanness of my hands" or "the LORD has repaid me according to my righteousness". Matthew 16:27 says it of "the Son of Man", and Revelation 22:12 "My reward is with Me"; in Proverbs 24:29 a man is told not to say "I will repay the man according to his work".

rows.title: Like a tree planted by streams of water

Psalms: Blessed is the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked

Elsewhere in the Old Testament: blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD

like a vine in your vineyard, planted by the water

rows.alike: Both say "blessed is the man" and go on "He is like a tree planted by" water, with leaves that stay fresh ("whose leaf does not wither"; "its leaves are always green") and fruit that keeps coming ("yielding its fruit in season"; "nor does it cease to produce fruit").
rows.different: Psalm 1:1 names the man by what he does not do, "does not walk in the counsel of the wicked", Jeremiah 17:7 by "who trusts in the LORD"; Jeremiah 17:8 adds "It does not fear when the heat comes" and "a year of drought". Ezekiel 19:10 says "planted by the water" of "a vine", "Your mother".

rows.title: There is no one who does good, not even one

Psalms: There is no one who does good.
to see if any understand, if any seek God

There is no one who does good.

no one alive is righteous before You
Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: there is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins
Elsewhere in the Old Testament: there is no one who does not sin
there is no one who does not sin
The letters & Revelation: Romans 3:10
There is no one righteous, not even one.
Romans 3:11
There is no one who understands, no one who seeks God.
Romans 3:12
All have turned away, they have together become worthless; there is no one who does good, not even one.

rows.alike: Psalm 14:3, Psalm 53:3 and Romans 3:12 share "All have turned away, they have together become" and "there is no one who does good, not even one"; Ecclesiastes 7:20 has "no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins", and 1 Kings 8:46 and 2 Chronicles 6:36 "there is no one who does not sin".
rows.different: Where the Psalms have "become corrupt", Romans 3:12 has "become worthless"; Psalms 14:2 and 53:2 have God looking "to see if any understand, if any seek God", where Romans 3:11 says "There is no one who understands, no one who seeks God". Romans 3:10 brings its words in with "As it is written" and begins "There is no one righteous"; 1 Kings 8:46 and 2 Chronicles 6:36 set the words inside "When they sin against You".

rows.title: Blessed is he whose transgressions are forgiven

Psalms: Blessed is he whose transgressions are forgiven, whose sins are covered.

The letters & Revelation: Romans 4:7
Blessed are they whose lawless acts are forgiven, whose sins are covered.
Romans 4:8
Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will never count against him.

rows.alike: Both say "Blessed" of those whose wrongs "are forgiven" and "whose sins are covered", and of "the man" whom the Lord does not "count against him".
rows.different: Psalm 32:1 has "transgressions", Romans 4:7 "lawless acts"; Psalm 32:2 says "does not count" and goes on "in whose spirit there is no deceit", where Romans 4:8 says "will never count" and stops there.

rows.title: In favor with God and man

Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: Then you will find favor and high regard in the sight of God and man.
Elsewhere in the Old Testament: in favor with the LORD and with man
Gospels & Acts: Jesus grew in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and man.
The letters & Revelation: 2 Corinthians 8:21
not only in the eyes of the Lord, but also in the eyes of men

rows.alike: 1 Samuel 2:26 "in favor with the LORD and with man", Proverbs 3:4 "favor and high regard in the sight of God and man" and Luke 2:52 "in favor with God and man" join favor with God and with man; 2 Corinthians 8:21 has "in the eyes of the Lord" and "in the eyes of men".
rows.different: 1 Samuel 2:26 and Luke 2:52 say it of one who grew ("the boy Samuel", "Jesus"), both with "stature" and Luke adding "wisdom"; Proverbs 3:4 says to the one addressed "Then you will find favor"; 2 Corinthians 8:21 is about "taking great care to do what is right".

rows.title: A pleasing aroma

The Law & history: When the LORD smelled the pleasing aroma
a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD
the food for My food offerings, as a pleasing aroma to Me
I will refuse to smell the pleasing aroma of your sacrifices
Psalms & wisdom: I will offer You fatlings as burnt offerings, with the fragrant smoke of rams
The Prophets: you set before them as a pleasing aroma the food I had given you
I will accept you as a pleasing aroma
The letters: gave Himself up for us as a fragrant sacrificial offering to God
They are a fragrant offering, an acceptable sacrifice, well-pleasing to God
we are to God the sweet aroma of Christ

rows.alike: In the Law a burnt offering is 'a pleasing aroma to the LORD' (Leviticus 1:9), and Genesis 8:21 has 'When the LORD smelled the pleasing aroma'; Ephesians 5:2 says Christ 'gave Himself up for us as a fragrant sacrificial offering to God', and Philippians 4:18 calls gifts received from Epaphroditus 'a fragrant offering, an acceptable sacrifice'.
rows.different: The aroma can be refused: 'I will refuse to smell the pleasing aroma of your sacrifices' (Leviticus 26:31), and Ezekiel 16:19 has 'you set before them as a pleasing aroma the food I had given you'. In Ezekiel 20:41 God says 'I will accept you as a pleasing aroma', and in 2 Corinthians 2:15 'we are to God the sweet aroma of Christ'.

rows.title: Without blemish

The Law & history: Your lamb must be an unblemished year-old male
he is to present an unblemished male
it must be without blemish or defect to be acceptable
an unblemished red heifer that has no defect
he is to present an unblemished male
he must bring an unblemished male goat as his offering
must offer an unblemished male from the cattle, sheep, or goats

The Prophets: an unblemished male goat as a sin offering
six unblemished male lambs and an unblemished ram
sacrifices a defective animal to the Lord
The letters: the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or spot
without stain or wrinkle or any such blemish, but holy and blameless
to present you holy, unblemished, and blameless in His presence
to present you unblemished in His glorious presence

rows.alike: The Law asks that an offering be 'without blemish or defect to be acceptable' (Leviticus 22:21), 'an unblemished male' (Leviticus 1:10; 22:19), or 'an unblemished male goat' (Leviticus 4:23); 1 Peter 1:19 speaks of 'the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or spot', and Hebrews 9:14 says Christ 'offered Himself unblemished to God'.
rows.different: In Malachi 1:14 the one who 'sacrifices a defective animal to the Lord' is called 'cursed'. Ephesians 5:27, Colossians 1:22 and Jude 1:24 use the word of people: 'without stain or wrinkle or any such blemish' (Ephesians 5:27), 'to present you holy, unblemished, and blameless in His presence' (Colossians 1:22), 'to present you unblemished in His glorious presence' (Jude 1:24).

rows.title: The blood is the life: do not eat it

The Law & history: you must not eat meat with its lifeblood still in it
the life of all flesh is its blood; whoever eats it must be cut off
Only be sure not to eat the blood, because the blood is the life
the troops are sinning against the LORD by eating meat with the blood still in it
The Prophets: You eat meat with the blood in it
Gospels & Acts: from the meat of strangled animals, and from blood
You must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood
they must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood

rows.alike: The Law forbids eating 'meat with its lifeblood still in it' (Genesis 9:4) and gives the reason 'the blood is the life' (Deuteronomy 12:23); 1 Samuel 14:33 and Ezekiel 33:25 name the same act, eating 'meat with the blood', and Acts 15:29 and 21:25 have 'abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood', the second of 'the Gentile believers'.
rows.different: Leviticus 17:14 adds 'whoever eats it must be cut off', and 1 Samuel 14:33 calls eating meat with the blood 'sinning against the LORD'. In Acts 15:20 'from blood' stands in a list beside 'food polluted by idols' and 'the meat of strangled animals'.

rows.title: It is the blood that makes atonement

The Law & history: I have given it to you to make atonement for your souls upon the altar; for it is the blood that makes atonement for the soul
The letters: nearly everything must be purified with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness
God presented Him as an atoning sacrifice in His blood through faith
by making peace through the blood of His cross
the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin

rows.alike: Leviticus 17:11 says 'it is the blood that makes atonement for the soul'; Hebrews 9:22 says 'without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness', and Romans 3:25 speaks of 'an atoning sacrifice in His blood'.
rows.different: Leviticus 17:11 says 'I have given it to you to make atonement for your souls upon the altar'; the letters say 'purified with blood' (Hebrews 9:22), 'making peace through the blood of His cross' (Colossians 1:20) and 'the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin' (1 John 1:7).

rows.title: To make atonement

The Law & history: the priest will make atonement on their behalf, and they will be forgiven
on this day atonement will be made for you to cleanse you
when atonement has been made for him, he will be forgiven
Psalms & wisdom: deliver us and atone for our sins, for the sake of Your name
By loving devotion and faithfulness iniquity is atoned for
The Prophets: Now that this has touched your lips, your iniquity is removed and your sin is atoned for
to make atonement for the house of Israel
to put an end to sin, to make atonement for iniquity
The letters: a merciful and faithful high priest in service to God, in order to make atonement for the sins of the people
He Himself is the atoning sacrifice for our sins
sent His Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins

rows.alike: In the Law 'the priest will make atonement on their behalf, and they will be forgiven' (Leviticus 4:20); Hebrews 2:17 uses the same words of 'a merciful and faithful high priest', 'to make atonement for the sins of the people', and Daniel 9:24 has 'to make atonement for iniquity'.
rows.different: Who atones differs: 'the priest' in Leviticus, God in the Psalms ('You atone for our transgressions', Psalm 65:3), and in Proverbs 16:6 'loving devotion and faithfulness'. In Isaiah 6:7 it happens when 'this has touched your lips'; 1 John 2:2 and 4:10 use the noun, 'the atoning sacrifice for our sins'.

rows.title: By His blood: purchased, redeemed, released

Gospels & Acts: the church of God, which He purchased with His own blood
The letters: we have now been justified by His blood
In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses
He entered the Most Holy Place once for all by His own blood, thus securing eternal redemption
it was not with perishable things such as silver or gold that you were redeemed
to sanctify the people by His own blood
Revelation: To Him who loves us and has released us from our sins by His blood
by Your blood You purchased for God those from every tribe and tongue and people and nation
They have conquered him by the blood of the Lamb

rows.alike: Acts 20:28 and Revelation 5:9 both say people were 'purchased' with His blood: 'which He purchased with His own blood', 'by Your blood You purchased for God'. Ephesians 1:7 and Hebrews 9:12 both speak of 'redemption' by His blood.
rows.different: Each names what the blood does in its own word: 'justified' (Romans 5:9), 'the forgiveness of our trespasses' (Ephesians 1:7), 'released us from our sins' (Revelation 1:5), 'conquered him' (Revelation 12:11), 'to sanctify the people' (Hebrews 13:12). What is purchased is 'the church of God' in Acts 20:28 and people 'from every tribe and tongue and people and nation' in Revelation 5:9.

rows.title: The blood of bulls and goats

The Law & history: He is to take some of the bull's blood and some of the goat's blood and put it on all the horns of the altar
Psalms & wisdom: Do I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?
The Prophets: I take no delight in the blood of bulls and lambs and goats
The letters: He did not enter by the blood of goats and calves
it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins
the blood of goats and bulls

rows.alike: Each speaks of the blood of bulls or goats: 'the blood of goats' (Psalm 50:13), 'the blood of bulls and lambs and goats' (Isaiah 1:11), 'the blood of bulls and goats' (Hebrews 10:4); in Leviticus 16:18 'the bull's blood and some of the goat's blood' are put 'on all the horns of the altar'.
rows.different: In Leviticus 16:18 the blood is put 'on all the horns of the altar'. In Psalm 50:13 God asks 'Do I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?', and in Isaiah 1:11 He says 'I take no delight in the blood of bulls and lambs and goats'. Hebrews 9:13 has 'the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those who are ceremonially unclean sanctify them so that their bodies are clean'; Hebrews 10:4 has 'it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins'; and Hebrews 9:12 has 'He did not enter by the blood of goats and calves'.

rows.title: Each day, once a year, once for all

The Law & history: This is what you are to offer regularly on the altar, each day: two lambs that are a year old
to make atonement once a year for the Israelites because of all their sins
Once a year Aaron shall make atonement on the horns of the altar
The Prophets: an unblemished year-old lamb as a daily burnt offering to the LORD; you are to offer it every morning
It magnified itself, even to the Prince of the host; it removed His daily sacrifice
The letters: He does not need to offer daily sacrifices
He sacrificed for sin once for all when He offered up Himself
only the high priest entered the second room, and then only once a year, and never without blood
He has appeared once for all at the end of the ages to do away with sin by the sacrifice of Himself
the sacrifice of the body of Jesus Christ once for all
Day after day every priest stands to minister and to offer again and again the same sacrifices
The death He died, He died to sin once for all
Christ also suffered for sins once for all

rows.alike: The Law sets offerings 'each day' (Exodus 29:38) and atonement 'once a year' (Leviticus 16:34; Exodus 30:10); Hebrews names the same measures: 'daily sacrifices' (7:27), 'once a year' (9:7) and 'Day after day' (10:11).
rows.different: Among these verses the words 'once for all' appear only in the letters: 'He sacrificed for sin once for all when He offered up Himself' (Hebrews 7:27), 'the sacrifice of the body of Jesus Christ once for all' (Hebrews 10:10), 'The death He died, He died to sin once for all' (Romans 6:10), 'Christ also suffered for sins once for all' (1 Peter 3:18); Hebrews 9:26 has 'He has appeared once for all'. Ezekiel 46:13 has 'an unblemished year-old lamb as a daily burnt offering to the LORD; you are to offer it every morning', and in Daniel 8:11 'It magnified itself' and 'removed His daily sacrifice'.

rows.title: The Passover lamb

The Law & history: select for yourselves a lamb for each family, and slaughter the Passover lamb
when I see the blood, I will pass over you
It is the Passover sacrifice to the LORD
You are to offer to the LORD your God the Passover sacrifice
the Passover lamb was slaughtered on the fourteenth day of the first month
the Levites slaughtered the Passover lamb for all the exiles
Gospels & Acts: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed
the day of Unleavened Bread on which the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed
The letters: For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed
By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of blood

rows.alike: The phrase 'the Passover lamb' runs from Exodus 12:21, 'slaughter the Passover lamb', through 2 Chronicles 35:1 and Ezra 6:20 to Mark 14:12 and Luke 22:7, where 'the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed'; 1 Corinthians 5:7 says 'Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed'.
rows.different: Exodus 12:27 calls it 'the Passover sacrifice to the LORD'; the Gospels name the day it 'was to be sacrificed'; among these verses only 1 Corinthians 5:7 names a person as 'our Passover lamb'. Hebrews 11:28 says 'By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of blood', and Exodus 12:13 has 'when I see the blood, I will pass over you'.

rows.title: Abraham offered Isaac on the altar

The Law & history: Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains
He bound his son Isaac and placed him on the altar, atop the wood
He split the wood for a burnt offering
Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and placed it on his son Isaac
The letters: By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac on the altar
Was not our father Abraham justified by what he did when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?

rows.alike: Genesis 22:9 tells how Abraham 'placed him on the altar'; Hebrews 11:17 and James 2:21 both say he 'offered' Isaac 'on the altar'.
rows.different: Genesis 22:2 gives God's command, 'Offer him there as a burnt offering'. Hebrews 11:17 says 'By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac on the altar' and calls Isaac 'his one and only son'; James 2:21 says 'our father Abraham' offered his son Isaac on the altar.

rows.title: Abel's offering and Cain's

The Law & history: the LORD looked with favor on Abel and his offering
but He had no regard for Cain and his offering
The letters: By faith Abel offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did. By faith he was commended as righteous when God gave approval to his gifts.

rows.alike: Both set Abel's offering against Cain's: 'the LORD looked with favor on Abel and his offering' (Genesis 4:4); 'Abel offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did' (Hebrews 11:4).
rows.different: Genesis 4:4-5 says the LORD 'looked with favor on Abel and his offering' and 'had no regard for Cain and his offering'; Hebrews 11:4 says 'By faith' and that Abel 'was commended as righteous'.

rows.title: A sin offering, a guilt offering

The Law & history: a young bull without blemish as a sin offering for the sin he has committed
he must bring his guilt offering to the LORD for the sin he has committed
the assembly must bring a young bull as a sin offering
Take for yourself a young bull for a sin offering
with a young bull for a sin offering
you are to take a second young bull for a sin offering
The Prophets: when His soul is made a guilt offering
a young bull from the herd as a sin offering
you are to provide a male goat daily for a sin offering
The letters: God did by sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful man, as an offering for sin
And where these have been forgiven, an offering for sin is no longer needed.
If we deliberately go on sinning after we have received the knowledge of the truth, no further sacrifice for sins remains

rows.alike: Leviticus has 'a sin offering' (4:3) and 'his guilt offering' (5:6); Isaiah 53:10 has 'when His soul is made a guilt offering', and Romans 8:3 has God 'sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful man, as an offering for sin'.
rows.different: Isaiah 53:10 uses the word of 'His soul', and Romans 8:3 of God's 'own Son'. Ezekiel 43:19 and 43:25 have 'a young bull from the herd as a sin offering' and 'a male goat daily for a sin offering'. Hebrews 10:18 says 'And where these have been forgiven, an offering for sin is no longer needed', and Hebrews 10:26 says 'If we deliberately go on sinning after we have received the knowledge of the truth, no further sacrifice for sins remains'.

rows.title: Outside the camp

The Law & history: burn the flesh of the bull and its hide and dung outside the camp; it is a sin offering
he is to take the bull outside the camp and burn it
whose blood was brought into the Most Holy Place to make atonement, must be taken outside the camp
he will have it brought outside the camp and slaughtered in his presence
The Prophets: take away the bull for the sin offering and burn it in the appointed part of the temple area outside the sanctuary
The letters: the high priest brings the blood of animals into the Holy Place as a sacrifice for sin, the bodies are burned outside the camp
Jesus also suffered outside the city gate, to sanctify the people by His own blood
let us go to Him outside the camp, bearing the disgrace He bore

rows.alike: The Law burns the sin offering's body 'outside the camp' when its blood has been 'brought into the Most Holy Place' (Leviticus 16:27); Hebrews 13:11 has both, 'the blood of animals into the Holy Place' and 'the bodies are burned outside the camp'.
rows.different: Ezekiel 43:21 has 'outside the sanctuary'. Hebrews 13:12 says Jesus 'suffered outside the city gate', and 13:13 calls its readers to 'go to Him outside the camp, bearing the disgrace He bore'.

rows.title: Sprinkled: blood, water, the ashes of a heifer

The Law & history: Seven times he shall sprinkle the one to be cleansed of the skin disease
sprinkle it with his finger on the east side of the mercy seat
gather up the ashes of the heifer
The man who is ceremonially clean is to sprinkle the unclean person
The Prophets: so He will sprinkle many nations
I will also sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean
The letters: the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those who are ceremonially unclean
he sprinkled with blood the tabernacle and all the vessels used in worship
having our hearts sprinkled to cleanse us from a guilty conscience
the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel
for obedience to Jesus Christ and sprinkling by His blood

rows.alike: Numbers 19:9 gathers 'the ashes of the heifer', and Hebrews 9:13 names 'the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those who are ceremonially unclean'; the Law sprinkles 'the one to be cleansed' (Leviticus 14:7), and Hebrews 10:22 speaks of 'hearts sprinkled to cleanse us'.
rows.different: In the Law the one to be cleansed is sprinkled (Leviticus 14:7; Numbers 19:19) and blood is sprinkled 'on the east side of the mercy seat' (Leviticus 16:14); Ezekiel 36:25 has God say 'I will also sprinkle clean water on you'; Isaiah 52:15 has 'He will sprinkle many nations'. In Hebrews 10:22 it is 'hearts' that are sprinkled, 'from a guilty conscience', and Hebrews 12:24 and 1 Peter 1:2 speak of 'sprinkled blood' and 'sprinkling by His blood'.

rows.title: With hyssop

The Law & history: Take a cluster of hyssop, dip it into the blood in the basin
two live clean birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop be brought for the one to be cleansed
take some hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle the tent
the hyssop growing in the wall
Psalms & wisdom: Purify me with hyssop, and I will be clean
Gospels & Acts: they soaked a sponge in the wine, put it on a stalk of hyssop
The letters: he took the blood of calves and goats, along with water, scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled the scroll and all the people

rows.alike: Hyssop is what blood or water is put on with: 'dip it into the blood' (Exodus 12:22), 'dip it in the water, and sprinkle' (Numbers 19:18), 'water, scarlet wool, and hyssop' (Hebrews 9:19); Psalm 51:7 prays 'Purify me with hyssop, and I will be clean'.
rows.different: Psalm 51:7 has 'Purify me with hyssop, and I will be clean; wash me, and I will be whiter than snow'. Leviticus 14:4 and Hebrews 9:19 add scarlet: 'scarlet yarn', 'scarlet wool'.

rows.title: Thank offerings and the sacrifice of praise

The Law & history: along with the sacrifice of thanksgiving he shall offer unleavened cakes mixed with olive oil
come near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the house of the LORD
sacrificed peace offerings and thank offerings on it
Psalms & wisdom: Sacrifice a thank offering to God
He who sacrifices a thank offering honors Me
Freely I will sacrifice to You; I will praise Your name
Let them offer sacrifices of thanksgiving and declare His works with rejoicing
I will offer to You a sacrifice of thanksgiving and call on the name of the LORD
I will render thank offerings to You
The Prophets: and thank offerings to the house of the LORD
the voices of those bringing thank offerings into the house of the LORD
But I, with the voice of thanksgiving, will sacrifice to You
that we may present the fruit of our lips
The letters: let us continually offer to God a sacrifice of praise, the fruit of lips that confess His name

rows.alike: Leviticus 7:12 has 'the sacrifice of thanksgiving'; the Psalms have 'a sacrifice of thanksgiving' (Psalm 116:17), and Jonah has 'with the voice of thanksgiving, will sacrifice to You'; Hebrews 13:15 has 'a sacrifice of praise, the fruit of lips', as Hosea 14:2 has 'the fruit of our lips'.
rows.different: In Leviticus 7:12 it comes with 'unleavened cakes mixed with olive oil'; in the Psalms it goes with words, 'declare His works' and 'call on the name of the LORD'; in Hebrews 13:15 it is offered 'continually' and is 'the fruit of lips that confess His name'.

rows.title: A broken spirit, a contrite heart

Psalms & wisdom: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, You will not despise
The LORD is near to the brokenhearted; He saves the contrite in spirit
The Prophets: I dwell in a high and holy place, and with the oppressed and humble in spirit, to restore the spirit of the lowly and revive the heart of the contrite
This is the one I will esteem: he who is humble and contrite in spirit, who trembles at My word

rows.alike: The shared word is 'contrite', with 'spirit' or 'heart': 'a broken and a contrite heart' (Psalm 51:17), 'the contrite in spirit' (Psalm 34:18), 'humble and contrite in spirit' (Isaiah 66:2), 'the heart of the contrite' (Isaiah 57:15).
rows.different: Only Psalm 51:17 calls it a sacrifice: 'The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit'. Psalm 34:18 says 'The LORD is near'; Isaiah 57:15 has God say 'I dwell' with them; Isaiah 66:2 'This is the one I will esteem'.

rows.title: Sacrifices of righteousness

The Law & history: They will call the peoples to a mountain; there they will offer sacrifices of righteousness
Psalms & wisdom: Offer the sacrifices of the righteous and trust in the LORD
Then You will delight in righteous sacrifices, in whole burnt offerings; then bulls will be offered on Your altar
The Prophets: He will purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and silver. Then they will present offerings to the LORD in righteousness

rows.alike: Each joins sacrifice to righteousness: 'sacrifices of righteousness' (Deuteronomy 33:19), 'the sacrifices of the righteous' (Psalm 4:5), 'righteous sacrifices' (Psalm 51:19), 'offerings to the LORD in righteousness' (Malachi 3:3).
rows.different: Psalm 4:5 is a command, 'Offer'. Deuteronomy 33:19, Psalm 51:19 and Malachi 3:3 speak of what will be: 'there they will offer', 'Then You will delight', 'Then they will present', Malachi's after He will 'purify the sons of Levi'.

rows.title: Better than sacrifice

The Law & history: Does the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as in obedience to His voice? Behold, obedience is better than sacrifice
Psalms & wisdom: To do righteousness and justice is more desirable to the LORD than sacrifice
Draw near to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools
I will praise God's name in song and exalt Him with thanksgiving
And this will please the LORD more than an ox
The Prophets: I did not merely command them about burnt offerings and sacrifices
but this is what I commanded them: Obey Me
Gospels & Acts: to love your neighbor as yourself. This is more important than all burnt offerings and sacrifices

rows.alike: Each sets something above sacrifice in a comparison: 'obedience is better than sacrifice' (1 Samuel 15:22), 'more desirable to the LORD than sacrifice' (Proverbs 21:3), 'more than an ox' (Psalm 69:31), 'more important than all burnt offerings and sacrifices' (Mark 12:33).
rows.different: What is set higher differs: 'obedience to His voice' (1 Samuel 15:22) and 'Obey Me' (Jeremiah 7:23), 'righteousness and justice' (Proverbs 21:3), 'to listen' (Ecclesiastes 5:1), praise 'with thanksgiving' (Psalm 69:30), and in Mark 12:33 the love of God and 'your neighbor as yourself'.

rows.title: Sacrifice and offering You did not desire

The Law & history: Does the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as in obedience to His voice
Psalms & wisdom: Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, but my ears You have opened. Burnt offerings and sin offerings You did not require.
For You do not delight in sacrifice, or I would bring it; You take no pleasure in burnt offerings.
The Prophets: What good to Me is your multitude of sacrifices?
Should I come to Him with burnt offerings, with year-old calves?
what does the LORD require of you but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?
The letters: when Christ came into the world, He said
Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, but a body You prepared for Me
In burnt offerings and sin offerings You took no delight.
although they are offered according to the law

rows.alike: 'Sacrifice and offering You did not desire' stands word for word in Psalm 40:6 and Hebrews 10:5; Psalm 51:16 'You do not delight in sacrifice' and Hebrews 10:6 'You took no delight' share the word 'delight'; Micah 6:8 asks 'what does the LORD require of you', where Psalm 40:6 says of burnt offerings 'You did not require'.
rows.different: Psalm 40:6 has 'my ears You have opened' where Hebrews 10:5 has 'a body You prepared for Me'; Hebrews 10:5 gives the words to Christ, 'when Christ came into the world, He said', and 10:8 has the note 'although they are offered according to the law'. Micah 6:8 has 'to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God'.

rows.title: I will not accept them

The Law & history: You must not present anything with a defect, because it will not be accepted on your behalf
Psalms & wisdom: The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable to the LORD
The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable-how much more so when brought with ill intent!
The Prophets: Bring your worthless offerings no more; your incense is detestable to Me
Your burnt offerings are not acceptable; your sacrifices do not please Me
although they may offer burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them
Even though you offer Me burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them
whatever they offer there is defiled
I will accept no offering from your hands
You bring offerings that are stolen, lame, or sick! Should I accept these from your hands?
He no longer regards your offerings or receives them gladly from your hands

rows.alike: Jeremiah 14:12 and Amos 5:22 say the same words of 'burnt offerings and grain offerings': 'I will not accept them'; Malachi 1:10 has 'I will accept no offering from your hands'. Proverbs 15:8 and 21:27 say 'The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable', and Isaiah 1:13 'your incense is detestable to Me'.
rows.different: Leviticus 22:20 gives the animal's 'defect' as the reason, and Malachi 1:13 offerings 'stolen, lame, or sick'; Proverbs names 'the wicked' and 'ill intent'. Jeremiah 14:12 and Amos 5:22 give no reason within the verse.

rows.title: Accepted, pleasing to God

The Law & history: so it can be accepted on his behalf to make atonement for him
in order for it to be accepted on your behalf
The Prophets: Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be accepted on My altar
Then the offerings of Judah and Jerusalem will please the LORD
The letters: to offer your bodies as living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God
offering spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ
do not neglect to do good and to share with others, for with such sacrifices God is pleased

rows.alike: The Law's words are 'accepted on his behalf' and 'accepted on your behalf' (Leviticus 1:4; 22:19), and Isaiah 56:7 has 'will be accepted on My altar'; the letters have 'pleasing to God' (Romans 12:1), 'acceptable to God' (1 Peter 2:5), 'God is pleased' (Hebrews 13:16).
rows.different: In the Law and the Prophets what is accepted is an animal or an offering, and in Ezekiel 43:27 God says 'I will accept you'. In the letters the sacrifices are 'your bodies' (Romans 12:1), 'spiritual sacrifices' (1 Peter 2:5), and 'to do good and to share with others' (Hebrews 13:16).

rows.title: Poured out like a drink offering

The Law & history: he poured out a drink offering on it and anointed it with oil
Pour out the offering of fermented drink to the LORD in the sanctuary area
a drink offering of a quarter hin of wine
nor are you to pour a drink offering on it
a quarter hin of wine as a drink offering
a third of a hin of wine as a drink offering
half a hin of wine as a drink offering
as well as a drink offering
Psalms & wisdom: Sorrows will multiply to those who chase other gods. I will not pour out their libations of blood
The Prophets: they pour out drink offerings to other gods to provoke Me to anger
Grain and drink offerings have been cut off from the house of the LORD
you have poured out a drink offering
The letters: even if I am being poured out like a drink offering on the sacrifice and service of your faith
For I am already being poured out like a drink offering, and the time of my departure is at hand

rows.alike: A drink offering is 'poured out': Jacob 'poured out a drink offering' (Genesis 35:14), and Numbers 28:7 says 'Pour out the offering of fermented drink'; Philippians 2:17 and 2 Timothy 4:6 use the same words of the writer: 'being poured out like a drink offering'.
rows.different: Exodus 30:9 says 'nor are you to pour a drink offering on it'; Jeremiah 7:18 has 'they pour out drink offerings to other gods', and Psalm 16:4 'I will not pour out their libations of blood'; Joel 1:9 says 'Grain and drink offerings have been cut off from the house of the LORD'. In the letters it is the writer who is poured out, in Philippians 2:17 'on the sacrifice and service of your faith', in 2 Timothy 4:6 as 'the time of my departure is at hand'.

rows.title: Sacrificed to demons, not to God

The Law & history: They must no longer offer their sacrifices to the goat demons
They sacrificed to demons, not to God
Psalms & wisdom: They sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons.
The letters: No, but the sacrifices of pagans are offered to demons, not to God. And I do not want you to be participants with demons.

rows.alike: Deuteronomy 32:17 'They sacrificed to demons, not to God' and 1 Corinthians 10:20 'offered to demons, not to God' share the words; Leviticus 17:7 and Psalm 106:37 also name sacrifices to demons.
rows.different: Psalm 106:37 says what was sacrificed, 'their sons and their daughters'. 1 Corinthians 10:20 speaks of 'the sacrifices of pagans' and adds 'I do not want you to be participants with demons'.

rows.title: Food sacrificed to idols

The Law & history: they will invite you, and you will eat their sacrifices
who also invited them to the sacrifices for their gods. And the people ate
Gospels & Acts: You must abstain from food sacrificed to idols
they must abstain from food sacrificed to idols
The letters: Now about food sacrificed to idols
So about eating food sacrificed to idols: We know that an idol is nothing at all in the world
then do not eat it, for the sake of the one who told you and for the sake of conscience
Revelation: the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to place a stumbling block before the Israelites so they would eat food sacrificed to idols
By her teaching she misleads My servants to be sexually immoral and to eat food sacrificed to idols

rows.alike: Exodus 34:15 and Numbers 25:2 speak of being invited to eat other gods' sacrifices; Acts 15:29, 1 Corinthians 8:1 and Revelation 2:14 and 2:20 use one phrase, 'food sacrificed to idols', and Revelation 2:14 names 'Balaam' and 'Balak'.
rows.different: Acts 15:29 says 'abstain', and Revelation 2:20 rebukes a teaching that 'misleads My servants' to eat it. 1 Corinthians 8:4 adds 'an idol is nothing at all in the world', and 10:28 says 'do not eat it' when told, 'for the sake of conscience'.

rows.title: Sons and daughters sacrificed in the fire

The Law & history: You must not give any of your children to be sacrificed to Molech
They even burn their sons and daughters in the fire as sacrifices to their gods
Let no one be found among you who sacrifices his son or daughter in the fire
he took his firstborn son, who was to succeed him, and offered him as a burnt offering on the city wall
even sacrificed his son in the fire
They sacrificed their sons and daughters in the fire
He sacrificed his own son in the fire
Psalms & wisdom: the blood of their sons and daughters, whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan
The Prophets: burn their sons and daughters in the fire-something I never commanded
to burn their children in the fire as offerings to Baal-something I never commanded or mentioned
to make their sons and daughters pass through the fire to Molech
You even took the sons and daughters you bore to Me and sacrificed them as food to idols
They have even sacrificed their children, whom they bore to Me, in the fire as food for their idols

rows.alike: The phrase recurs: 'their sons and daughters in the fire' (Deuteronomy 12:31; 2 Kings 17:17; Jeremiah 7:31), with 'to Molech' in Leviticus 18:21 and Jeremiah 32:35.
rows.different: The Law forbids it ('Let no one be found among you', Deuteronomy 18:10); Kings reports it done; Jeremiah adds God's words 'something I never commanded'; Ezekiel 16:20 calls the children 'sons and daughters you bore to Me' and the offering 'food to idols', and 23:37 has 'whom they bore to Me' and 'food for their idols'.

rows.title: Atonement for the altar; whatever touches it is holy

The Law & history: For seven days you shall make atonement for the altar and consecrate it. Then the altar will become most holy; whatever touches the altar will be holy.

rows.alike: "Love one another" (John 13:34, 15:17) and "we should love one another" (1 John 3:11, 3:23); "a new commandment" in John 13:34 and 1 John 2:8.

rows.title: Speak truth to one another

The Law & history: You must not lie or deceive one another.

rows.title: The fellowship

rows.title: Sin desires you: let it not rule

Psalms & wisdom: Keep Your servant also from willful sins; may they not rule over me

rows.alike: Each speaks of sin as something that would rule a person: it "desires you" (Genesis 4:7), "may they not rule over me" (Psalm 19:13), "let no sin rule over me" (Psalm 119:133), "do not let sin reign" (Romans 6:12), "sin shall not be your master" (Romans 6:14).

rows.alike: Each speaks of the heart as evil, deceitful or darkened: "every inclination of his heart is evil" (Genesis 8:21), "the hearts of men are full of evil" (Ecclesiastes 9:3), "the hearts of men become fully set on doing evil" (Ecclesiastes 8:11), "The heart is deceitful above all things" (Jeremiah 17:9), "his evil heart" (Jeremiah 16:12), "from within the hearts of men come evil thoughts" (Mark 7:21), "darkened in their foolish hearts" (Romans 1:21).
rows.different: Genesis 6:5 says what "the LORD saw", "all the time", and 8:21 what He "said in His heart"; Ecclesiastes 8:11 begins "When the sentence for a crime is not speedily executed"; Jeremiah 16:12 says "each of you follows the stubbornness of his evil heart instead of obeying Me", and 18:12 is what "they will reply", "each of us will act according to the stubbornness of his evil heart"; Jeremiah 17:9 asks "Who can understand it?"; Hebrews warns "none of you" to have "a wicked heart of unbelief".

The Law & history: they are indeed a stiff-necked people

rows.different: In Exodus 32:9 the LORD says it to Moses; in Exodus 34:9 it is part of a plea, "forgive our iniquity and sin"; Proverbs 29:1 says it of "A man" who "will suddenly be shattered beyond recovery"; in Acts 7:51 it is said to those addressed, who "always resist the Holy Spirit, just as your fathers did".

The Law & history: Only do not rebel against the LORD

rows.different: Numbers 20:24 says it of Aaron and of the one spoken to, "both of you"; in Isaiah 1:2 the speaker says "I have raised children"; Lamentations 1:18 ("yet I rebelled against His command") and Daniel 9:9 ("we have rebelled against Him") are in the first person; Hebrews 3:16 asks it of "all those Moses led out of Egypt".

The same charges are also made singly or together: "they have forsaken Me to worship Ashtoreth" (1 Kings 11:33), "You have forsaken Me" (2 Chronicles 12:5; Jeremiah 15:6), "Judah had forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers" (2 Chronicles 24:24), "burning incense to other gods" (Jeremiah 44:8; 44:15).
rows.different: 1 Samuel 12:10 is the people's own confession; Jeremiah 2:13 and 17:13 call the LORD "the fountain of living water"; Jeremiah 5:19 sets serving "foreign gods in your land" beside serving "foreigners in a land that is not your own"; 2 Chronicles 12:5 and 24:20 answer it, "I have forsaken you" and "He has forsaken you"; Jeremiah 5:7 says "gods that are not gods".

rows.different: Deuteronomy 32:21 is in the first person, "They have provoked My jealousy by that which is not God"; 1 Kings 14:22 says Judah "provoked Him to jealous anger more than all their fathers had done"; in Ezekiel 8:3 the speaker is carried "in visions of God to Jerusalem, to the entrance of the north gate of the inner court", where the idol "was seated"; 1 Corinthians 10:22 goes on "Are we stronger than He?". rows.alike: The same phrase is used of Israel, of Solomon and of Zedekiah: "did evil in the sight of the LORD" (Judges 2:11; 1 Kings 11:6; 2 Kings 24:19); close wording is used in "done what is evil in Your sight" (Psalm 51:4) and "you did evil in My sight" (Isaiah 65:12).
rows.different: In Judges 2:11, 1 Kings 11:6 and 2 Kings 24:19 it is told of others; in Psalm 51:4 the speaker says it of himself, "Against You, You only, have I sinned"; in Isaiah 65:12, 66:4 and Jeremiah 7:30 it is said in the first person, "in My sight" (Jeremiah 7:30 adds "declares the LORD"). 2 Kings 24:19 and Jeremiah 52:2 are word for word the same.

rows.alike: The same words of confession, "We have sinned" and "I have sinned", and one fuller form: "We have sinned and done wrong; we have acted wickedly" (1 Kings 8:47; 2 Chronicles 6:37), with small changes in "We have sinned like our fathers; we have done wrong and acted wickedly" (Psalm 106:6) and "we have sinned and done wrong. The short forms recur: "I have sinned" (Exodus 9:27; Numbers 22:34; 1 Samuel 15:30) and "We have sinned" (Numbers 21:7; Judges 10:15; Lamentations 3:42); Daniel 9:15 has "we have sinned; we have acted wickedly".

(Proverbs 20:9), "How can one born of woman be pure?" rows.different: Proverbs 20:9, Job 15:14 and Job 25:4 are put as questions; 1 John 1:8 and 1:10 put it as "If we say"; Romans 3:23 states "all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God" and 3:9 names "Jews and Greeks alike"; Galatians 3:22 says "the Scripture pronounces all things confined by sin".

For since death came through a man
For as in Adam all die

rows.alike: Genesis records of Adam "and then he died"; Romans and 1 Corinthians name Adam, or "one man", with death: "death reigned from Adam" (Romans 5:14), "in Adam all die" (1 Corinthians 15:22).
rows.different: Genesis gives Adam's years and his death; Romans 5:12 speaks of sin and death entering "through one man" and of death passed "to all men, because all sinned"; 1 Corinthians 15:21-22 speaks of death "through a man" and "in Adam".

rows.title: The serpent deceived

The Law & history: Now the serpent was more crafty than any beast of the field
The letters: Eve was deceived by the serpent's cunning
it was not Adam who was deceived, but the woman who was deceived and fell into transgression

rows.alike: Each speaks of the serpent's craft or of deceiving: "more crafty" (Genesis 3:1), "The serpent deceived me" (Genesis 3:13), "Eve was deceived by the serpent's cunning" (2 Corinthians 11:3), "the woman who was deceived" (1 Timothy 2:14).
rows.different: In Genesis the woman says it to the LORD God, "and I ate"; 2 Corinthians uses it of a fear that "your minds may be led astray"; 1 Timothy sets "not Adam" beside "the woman".

rows.title: Naked, and the shame of it

The Law & history: And the man and his wife were both naked, and they were not ashamed
they knew that they were naked; so they sewed together fig leaves and made coverings for themselves
I was afraid because I was naked; so I hid myself
The Prophets: Your nakedness will be uncovered and your shame will be exposed
Jerusalem has sinned greatly; therefore she has become an object of scorn. All who honored her now despise her, for they have seen her nakedness
and they will see you completely naked
I will show your nakedness to the nations and your shame to the kingdoms
Revelation: wretched, pitiful, poor, blind, and naked
white garments so that you may be clothed and your shameful nakedness not exposed
so that he will not go naked and let his shame be exposed

rows.alike: Each joins nakedness to shame, fear or covering it: "naked, and they were not ashamed" (Genesis 2:25), "so I hid myself" (Genesis 3:10), "Your nakedness will be uncovered and your shame will be exposed" (Isaiah 47:3), "your shameful nakedness not exposed" (Revelation 3:18).
rows.different: Genesis tells it of "the man and his wife"; Isaiah 47:3 goes on "I will take vengeance; I will spare no one"; Lamentations 1:8 says it after "Jerusalem has sinned greatly"; Ezekiel 16:37 says "they will see you completely naked" and Nahum 3:5 "I will show your nakedness to the nations"; Revelation 3:17-18 sets "I am rich" beside "wretched, pitiful, poor, blind, and naked" and counsels "white garments", and 16:15 says "Blessed is the one who remains awake and clothed".

rows.title: Thorns and thistles, and the cursed ground

The Law & history: Both thorns and thistles it will yield for you
the ground that the LORD has cursed
The Prophets: it is the sin of Israel; thorns and thistles will overgrow their altars
Gospels & Acts: Are grapes gathered from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
The letters: But land that produces thorns and thistles is worthless, and its curse is imminent

rows.alike: In all three "thorns and thistles" are named: "it will yield for you" (Genesis 3:18), "will overgrow their altars" (Hosea 10:8), "land that produces thorns and thistles" (Hebrews 6:8); Genesis 5:29 speaks of "the ground that the LORD has cursed" and Hebrews 6:8 of land whose "curse is imminent".
rows.different: Genesis 3:18 is said in the second person, "for you", and goes on "you will eat the plants of the field"; Hosea 10:8 sets it with the high places of Aven, "it is the sin of Israel"; Hebrews 6:8 adds "is worthless" and "In the end it will be burned". Matthew 7:16 uses thistles of knowing people by their fruit, another subject; Isaiah 10:17 has a fire "devour Assyria's thorns and thistles", also another subject.

rows.title: You will surely die

The Law & history: for in the day that you eat of it, you will surely die
be aware that you will surely die-you and all who belong to you
the LORD had told them that they would surely die in the wilderness
because by this deed you have shown utter contempt for the word of the LORD, the son born to you will surely die
The Prophets: Since he has committed all these abominations, he will surely die

rows.alike: The same words of a death sentence, "you will surely die", are given for a deed: eating from the tree (Genesis 2:17), not restoring a man's wife (Genesis 20:7), "this deed" (2 Samuel 12:14), "all these abominations" (Ezekiel 18:13); it is said to Ahimelech (1 Samuel 22:16) and, as what "the LORD says", to King Ahaziah (2 Kings 1:6; 1:16).
rows.different: The serpent denies it, "You will not surely die" (Genesis 3:4); in Ezekiel 33:14 the sentence is followed by "and he turns from his sin and does what is just and right"; in Jeremiah 26:8 "the priests and prophets and all the people" seize one who had "finished telling all the people everything the LORD had commanded him to say" and shout "You must surely die!"; in Ezekiel 3:18 and 33:8 it is a case, "If I say to the wicked man", and the one who does not warn is held "responsible for his blood" (3:18) or "accountable for his blood" (33:8).

rows.title: He will die in his iniquity; you will die in your sins

The Law & history: Instead, he died because of his own sin
The Prophets: that wicked man will die in his iniquity
he will die in his iniquity, but you will have saved yourself
If you did not warn him, he will die in his sin
that one will be taken away in his iniquity
then that wicked man will die in his iniquity
he will die in his iniquity, but you will have saved your life
Because of the unfaithfulness and sin he has committed, he will die
He will die because of the iniquity he has committed
Gospels & Acts: but you will die in your sin
That is why I told you that you would die in your sins

rows.alike: The same words, dying "in" or "because of" one's own sin: "he will die in his iniquity" (Ezekiel 3:19), "he will die in his sin" (Ezekiel 3:20), "he died because of his own sin" (Numbers 27:3), "you will die in your sin" (John 8:21).
rows.different: Numbers 27:3 is said of "Our father", who "was not among the followers of Korah"; Ezekiel 3:18-20 speaks of "a wicked man" and of "a righteous man" who "turns from his righteousness", and 33:6 of "the watchman"; John 8:21 has "I am going away, and you will look for Me", and 8:24 "For unless you believe that I am He, you will die in your sins".

rows.title: The soul who sins is the one who will die; the wages of sin is death

Psalms & wisdom: Genuine righteousness leads to life, but the pursuit of evil brings death
The Prophets: The soul who sins is the one who will die
The letters: The outcome of those things is death
For the wages of sin is death
it produced death in me through what was good
the law of sin and death
The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law
and sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death

rows.alike: Each joins sin, or evil, to death: "the pursuit of evil brings death" (Proverbs 11:19), "The soul who sins is the one who will die" (Ezekiel 18:4), "the wages of sin is death" (Romans 6:23), "sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death" (James 1:15).
rows.different: Ezekiel 18:4 adds "every soul belongs to Me; both father and son are Mine"; Proverbs 11:19 and Romans 6:23 each set death beside life, "righteousness leads to life" and "the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord"; Romans 7:13 says "it produced death in me through what was good"; 1 Corinthians 15:56 adds "the power of sin is the law".

rows.title: Dead, and alive

Gospels & Acts: For this son of mine was dead and is alive again!
this brother of yours was dead and is alive again
he has crossed over from death to life
The letters: And you were dead in your trespasses and sins
made us alive with Christ even when we were dead in our trespasses
When you were dead in your trespasses and in the uncircumcision of your sinful nature, God made you alive with Christ
count yourselves dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus
as those who have been brought from death to life
But she who lives for pleasure is dead even while she is still alive
We know that we have passed from death to life
Revelation: you have a reputation for being alive, yet you are dead

rows.alike: Each speaks of being "dead" or of "death", and all but Ephesians 2:1 set it beside "alive" or "life": "was dead and is alive again" (Luke 15:24), "dead in our trespasses" and "made us alive" (Ephesians 2:5), "from death to life" (John 5:24; 1 John 3:14), "alive, yet you are dead" (Revelation 3:1).
rows.different: In Luke 15 one speaks of "this son of mine" and "this brother of yours", adding "He was lost and is found"; Ephesians 2:1 and Colossians 2:13 say "dead in your trespasses"; Romans 6:11 says "dead to sin"; 1 John 3:14 gives "because we love our brothers" and "The one who does not love remains in death"; 1 Timothy 5:6 says "she who lives for pleasure is dead even while she is still alive", and Revelation 3:1 "you have a reputation for being alive, yet you are dead".

rows.title: Fallen asleep

Psalms & wisdom: Give light to my eyes, lest I sleep in death
so a man lies down and does not rise. Until the heavens are no more, he will not be awakened or roused from sleep
The Prophets: then they will fall asleep forever and never wake up
Then they will fall asleep forever and not wake up
Gospels & Acts: The girl is not dead, but asleep
The child is not dead, but asleep
she is not dead but asleep
Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going there to wake him up
They thought that Jesus was talking about actual sleep, but He was speaking about the death of Lazarus
the bodies of many saints who had fallen asleep were raised
And when he had said this, he fell asleep
The letters: those also who have fallen asleep in Christ
the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep
a number of you have fallen asleep
God will bring with Jesus those who have fallen asleep in Him
Ever since our fathers fell asleep

rows.alike: Each speaks of sleep or of falling asleep: "lest I sleep in death" (Psalm 13:3), "fall asleep forever" (Jeremiah 51:39), "not dead, but asleep" (Matthew 9:24), "he fell asleep" (Acts 7:60), "those who sleep in death" (1 Thessalonians 4:13).
rows.different: Job 14:12 says "Until the heavens are no more, he will not be awakened or roused from sleep", and Jeremiah 51:39 has "I will make them drunk" before "they will fall asleep forever and never wake up"; Jesus says "I am going there to wake him up", and John 11:13 adds "They thought that Jesus was talking about actual sleep"; 1 Corinthians 11:30 has "many among you are weak and sick, and a number of you have fallen asleep"; 1 Thessalonians 4:13 says "those who sleep in death" and "the rest, who are without hope".

rows.title: Gathered to his people; with his fathers

The Law & history: he breathed his last and died, old and contented, and was gathered to his people
Then he breathed his last and died and was gathered to his people, old and full of years
breathed his last, and he was gathered to his people
You will soon rest with your fathers
you will die and be gathered to your people
After that whole generation had also been gathered to their fathers
Then David rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David
And Solomon rested with his fathers
I will indeed gather you to your fathers, and you will be gathered to your grave in peace
Psalms & wisdom: he will join the generation of his fathers, who will never see the light of day
Gospels & Acts: His body was buried with his fathers and saw decay
the patriarch David died and was buried, and his tomb is with us to this day

rows.alike: All but Acts 2:29 speak of a death with "people" or "fathers": "gathered to his people" (Genesis 25:8), "gathered to their fathers" (Judges 2:10), "rested with his fathers" (1 Kings 2:10), "join the generation of his fathers" (Psalm 49:19), "buried with his fathers" (Acts 13:36); Acts 2:29 says only that David "died and was buried".
rows.different: Genesis 25:8 and 35:29 add "old and contented" and "old and full of years"; Deuteronomy 32:50 adds "just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people"; 2 Kings 22:20 has "you will be gathered to your grave in peace"; Psalm 49:19 adds "who will never see the light of day"; Acts 13:36 says of David "His body was buried with his fathers and saw decay", and Acts 2:29 "his tomb is with us to this day".

rows.title: Who can praise You from Sheol?

Psalms & wisdom: For there is no mention of You in death; who can praise You from Sheol?
Will the dust praise You? Will it proclaim Your faithfulness?
Do You work wonders for the dead? Do departed spirits rise up to praise You?
Can Your loving devotion be proclaimed in the grave, Your faithfulness in Abaddon?
It is not the dead who praise the LORD, nor any who descend into silence
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing
for in Sheol, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom
The Prophets: For Sheol cannot thank You; Death cannot praise You. Those who descend to the Pit cannot hope for Your faithfulness
The living, only the living, can thank You, as I do today

rows.alike: Most ask whether the dead praise, or say they do not: "who can praise You from Sheol?" (Psalm 6:5), "It is not the dead who praise the LORD" (Psalm 115:17), "Death cannot praise You" (Isaiah 38:18); "Your faithfulness" is named in Psalm 30:9, Psalm 88:11 and Isaiah 38:18 and 38:19.
rows.different: Psalm 30:9 has "my descent to the Pit" and Psalm 115:17 "nor any who descend into silence"; Isaiah 38:19 says "The living, only the living, can thank You, as I do today"; Ecclesiastes does not mention praise: "the dead know nothing", and "in Sheol, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom".

rows.title: Scattered among the nations

The Law & history: But I will scatter you among the nations
Then the LORD will scatter you among the peoples, and only a few of you will survive among the nations
Then the LORD will scatter you among all the nations, from one end of the earth to the other
The LORD will bring you and the king you appoint to a nation neither you nor your fathers have known
If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the nations
There is a certain people scattered and dispersed among the peoples of every province of your kingdom
Psalms & wisdom: You have scattered us among the nations
to disperse their offspring among the nations and scatter them throughout the lands
The Prophets: I will scatter them among the nations that neither they nor their fathers have known
So I will cast you out of this land into a land that neither you nor your fathers have known
when I disperse them among the nations and scatter them throughout the countries
I would scatter them among the nations and disperse them throughout the lands
I will disperse you among the nations and scatter you throughout the lands
I dispersed them among the nations, and they were scattered throughout the lands
And I will disperse the Egyptians among the nations and scatter them throughout the countries
you are scattered among the nations and throughout the lands
I will disperse the Egyptians among the nations and scatter them throughout the lands
I will disperse the Egyptians among the nations and scatter them throughout the lands
Gospels & Acts: where the Jews are dispersed among the Greeks

rows.alike: The same words recur, "scatter" and "disperse" "among the nations": "I will scatter you among the nations" (Leviticus 26:33; Nehemiah 1:8), "You have scattered us among the nations" (Psalm 44:11), "I dispersed them among the nations" (Ezekiel 36:19), "when you are scattered among the nations" (Ezekiel 6:8); and "neither you nor your fathers have known" (Deuteronomy 28:36; Jeremiah 16:13), "neither they nor their fathers have known" (Jeremiah 9:16).
rows.different: Leviticus 26:33 has "I will scatter you", Deuteronomy 4:27 "the LORD will scatter you among the peoples, and only a few of you will survive"; Nehemiah 1:8 recalls "the word that You commanded Your servant Moses"; Psalm 44:11 says "You have given us up as sheep to be devoured"; Esther 3:8 is Haman's word to the king; Ezekiel 29:12, 30:23 and 30:26 are said of "the Egyptians"; John 7:35 is what "the Jews said to one another" of "Him": "Where does He intend to go that we will not find Him?"

rows.title: Wanderers among the nations, with no place to rest

The Law & history: You will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth
from Your face I will be hidden; I will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth
He made them wander in the wilderness forty years, until the whole generation who had done evil in His sight was gone
Among those nations you will find no repose, not even a resting place for the sole of your foot
But the dove found no place to rest her foot
Psalms & wisdom: May his children wander as beggars
The Prophets: My God will reject them because they have not obeyed Him; and they shall be wanderers among the nations
she dwells among the nations but finds no place to rest
The letters: They wandered in deserts and mountains

rows.alike: Each speaks of wandering or of finding no rest, apart from the two cells marked aside: "a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth" (Genesis 4:12), "wanderers among the nations" (Hosea 9:17), "no repose, not even a resting place" among the nations (Deuteronomy 28:65), "finds no place to rest" (Lamentations 1:3).
rows.different: Genesis 4:12 and 4:14 have "from Your face I will be hidden" and "whoever finds me will kill me"; Numbers 32:13 says "He made them wander in the wilderness forty years"; Psalm 109:10 wishes it on "his children"; Lamentations 1:3 tells it as having happened, "Judah has gone into exile", and 4:15 adds "They can stay here no longer". Genesis 8:9 (the dove) and Hebrews 11:38 ("The world was not worthy of them") use the words of another subject.

rows.title: Cast out of His presence

The Law & history: and He removed them from His presence
until He had banished them from His presence
I will remove Judah from My sight, just as I removed Israel
until He finally banished them from His presence
Psalms & wisdom: Cast me not away from Your presence
The Prophets: And I will cast you out of My presence, just as I have cast out all your brothers
I will surely forget you and will cast you out of My presence
until He finally banished them from His presence

rows.alike: The same words, being removed or cast out of the LORD's presence: "He removed them from His presence" (2 Kings 17:18), "He finally banished them from His presence" (2 Kings 24:20; Jeremiah 52:3), "I will cast you out of My presence" (Jeremiah 7:15), "Cast me not away from Your presence" (Psalm 51:11).
rows.different: Kings tells it of Israel and then Judah, "just as I removed Israel"; 2 Kings 24:20 and Jeremiah 52:3 are word for word the same; Jeremiah 7:15 adds "just as I have cast out all your brothers, all the descendants of Ephraim", and 23:39 "I will surely forget you"; Psalm 51:11 is a request, "Cast me not away from Your presence; take not Your Holy Spirit from me".

rows.title: Into exile for their unfaithfulness

The Law & history: All this happened because the people of Israel had sinned against the LORD their God
But they were unfaithful to the God of their fathers
But Judah was exiled to Babylon because of their unfaithfulness
Because of our iniquities, we and our kings and priests have been delivered into the hands of the kings of the earth and subjected to the sword and to captivity
The Prophets: the house of Israel went into exile for their iniquity, because they were unfaithful to Me
in all the countries to which You have driven us because of our unfaithfulness to You
For the LORD has brought her grief because of her many transgressions. Her children have gone away as captives before the enemy

rows.alike: Each speaks of unfaithfulness, iniquity or sin, mostly with "because": "because of their unfaithfulness" (1 Chronicles 9:1), "because they were unfaithful to Me" (Ezekiel 39:23), "because of our unfaithfulness to You" (Daniel 9:7), "Because of our iniquities" (Ezra 9:7), "because of her many transgressions" (Lamentations 1:5), "because the people of Israel had sinned against the LORD their God" (2 Kings 17:7).
rows.different: Kings and Chronicles say "All this happened" (2 Kings 17:7) and "Judah was exiled to Babylon" (1 Chronicles 9:1); Ezra 9:7 and Daniel 9:7 say "we" and "our"; Ezekiel 39:23 gives it as what "the nations will know"; Lamentations 1:5 says "the LORD has brought her grief" and "Her children have gone away as captives before the enemy".

rows.title: Carried away into exile, away from its own land

The Law & history: carried away the Israelites to Assyria
So Israel was exiled from their homeland into Assyria, where they are to this day
to take the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh into exile
He took them into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon
So Judah was taken into exile, away from its own land
the exiles carried away to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar its king
carried away the people to Babylon
He had been carried into exile from Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon
The Prophets: So Judah was taken into exile, away from its own land
to all the exiles who were carried away from Jerusalem to Babylon
After Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah
and Israel will surely go into exile, away from their homeland
And Israel will surely go into exile, away from their homeland
carried Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon
Nebuchadnezzar had carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon
all you exiles I have sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon
your sons have been taken into exile
Gospels & Acts: at the time of the exile to Babylon
fourteen from David to the exile to Babylon, and fourteen from the exile to the Christ

rows.alike: The same words, "into exile" and "carried away", with the places named: "to Assyria" (2 Kings 17:6), "to Babylon" (2 Kings 24:15; Jeremiah 27:20; 29:1; 29:4), and "away from its own land" (2 Kings 25:21; Jeremiah 52:27), "away from their homeland" (Amos 7:11).
rows.different: Amos says it beforehand, "Israel will surely go into exile"; Kings, Chronicles, Ezra and Esther tell it after; 2 Kings 25:21 and Jeremiah 52:27 are word for word the same; Matthew uses "the exile to Babylon" to mark the generations; Jeremiah 48:46 says it of Moab, "your sons have been taken into exile".

rows.title: By the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept

The Law & history: When I heard these words, I sat down and wept
Now I assembled these exiles at the canal that flows to Ahava
Psalms & wisdom: By the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept when we remembered Zion
How can we sing a song of the LORD in a foreign land?
The Prophets: while I was among the exiles by the River Kebar
I came to the exiles at Tel-abib who dwelt by the River Kebar. And for seven days I sat where they sat

rows.alike: Most speak of exiles by water or of sitting in grief: "By the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept" (Psalm 137:1), "among the exiles by the River Kebar" (Ezekiel 1:1), "I sat where they sat" (Ezekiel 3:15), "I sat down and wept" (Nehemiah 1:4), "these exiles at the canal that flows to Ahava" (Ezra 8:15).
rows.different: Psalm 137:1 adds "when we remembered Zion", and 137:4 asks "How can we sing a song of the LORD in a foreign land?"; Ezekiel 1:1 has "I saw visions of God" while "among the exiles by the River Kebar"; Nehemiah 1:4 weeps "When I heard these words" and "mourned for days, fasting and praying"; Ezra 8:15 has "we camped there three days".

rows.title: I will hide My face; your sins have hidden His face

The Law & history: I will abandon them and hide My face from them
I will surely hide My face because of all the evil they have done by turning to other gods
I will hide My face from them; I will see what will be their end
Psalms & wisdom: Hide Your face from my sins and blot out all my iniquities
The Prophets: But your iniquities have built barriers between you and your God, and your sins have hidden His face from you, so that He does not hear
Your iniquities have diverted these from you; your sins have deprived you of My bounty
I was enraged by his sinful greed, so I struck him and hid My face in anger
I have hidden My face from this city because of all its wickedness
I dealt with them according to their uncleanness and transgressions, and I hid My face from them
At that time He will hide His face from them because of the evil they have done
In a surge of anger I hid My face from you for a moment
And I will no longer hide My face from them
I did not hide My face from scorn and spittle

rows.alike: Most speak of the LORD hiding His face, and several tie it to sin: "because of all the evil they have done by turning to other gods" (Deuteronomy 31:18), "because of the evil they have done" (Micah 3:4), "because of all its wickedness" (Jeremiah 33:5), "your sins have hidden His face from you" (Isaiah 59:2).
rows.different: Most are the LORD speaking, "I will hide My face"; Isaiah 59:2 has "your iniquities have built barriers between you and your God"; Jeremiah 5:25 does not mention a face: "your sins have deprived you of My bounty"; in Psalm 51:9 the speaker asks God to hide His face "from my sins"; Isaiah 54:8 says "In a surge of anger I hid My face from you for a moment" and Ezekiel 39:29 "I will no longer hide My face from them". Isaiah 50:6 uses the words of another subject: "I did not hide My face from scorn and spittle".

rows.title: He gave them over

The Law & history: He delivered them into the hands of those who plundered them
So You delivered them into the hands of enemies who oppressed them
Yet they would not listen, so You gave them into the hands of the neighboring peoples
Psalms & wisdom: When your children sinned against Him, He gave them over to their rebellion
So I gave them up to their stubborn hearts to follow their own devices
He delivered them into the hand of the nations
The Prophets: I also gave them over to statutes that were not good and ordinances by which they could not live
The letters: Therefore God gave them over in the desires of their hearts to impurity
For this reason God gave them over to dishonorable passions
He gave them up to a depraved mind

rows.alike: The same words of God handing people over: "He gave them over to their rebellion" (Job 8:4), "I gave them up to their stubborn hearts" (Psalm 81:12), "God gave them over in the desires of their hearts" (Romans 1:24), and into enemies' hands, "He delivered them into the hand of the nations" (Psalm 106:41).
rows.different: Judges 2:14, Nehemiah 9:27 and 9:30 and Psalm 106:41 speak of being given into the hands of enemies and nations; Job 8:4 says "When your children sinned against Him"; Psalm 81:12 is in the first person, "I gave them up"; Ezekiel 20:25 has "statutes that were not good and ordinances by which they could not live"; Romans 1:24, 26 and 28 say it three times, and 1:28 gives "since they did not see fit to acknowledge God".

rows.title: The iniquity of the fathers on the children

The Law & history: visiting the iniquity of the fathers on their children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me
visiting the iniquity of the fathers on their children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me
He will visit the iniquity of the fathers on their children and grandchildren to the third and fourth generations
He will visit the iniquity of the fathers upon their children to the third and fourth generation
The Prophets: but lay the iniquity of the fathers into the laps of their children after them
Our fathers sinned and are no more, but we bear their punishment

rows.alike: The same words, "the iniquity of the fathers" and "their children" (Exodus 20:5; Deuteronomy 5:9; Exodus 34:7; Numbers 14:18; Jeremiah 32:18), and in Lamentations "Our fathers sinned ... we bear their punishment".
rows.different: Exodus 20:5 and Deuteronomy 5:9 follow "You shall not bow down to them or worship them" and add "of those who hate Me"; Exodus 34:7 and Numbers 14:18 follow "forgiving iniquity" and continue "Yet He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished"; Exodus 34:7 adds "and grandchildren"; Jeremiah 32:18 says "You show loving devotion to thousands but lay the iniquity of the fathers into the laps of their children after them"; Lamentations 5:7 speaks as "we", of "Our fathers" who "are no more".

rows.title: The Judge of all the earth

The Law & history: Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?
May the LORD, the Judge, decide today
Psalms & wisdom: I could only beg my Judge for mercy
I would be delivered forever from my Judge
There is surely a God who judges the earth!
Rise up, O Judge of the earth
The Prophets: the LORD is our Judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our King
Gospels & Acts: There is One who seeks it, and He is the Judge.
The letters: There is only one Lawgiver and Judge
the Judge is standing at the door!
