As the Father has loved Me, so have I loved you
You loved Me before the foundation of the world
The letters: the kingdom of His beloved Son

rows.alike: Each speaks of love toward the Son: "The Father loves the Son" (John 3:35, 5:20), "As the Father has loved Me" (John 15:9), "His beloved Son" (Colossians 1:13).
rows.different: John 10:17 gives a reason: "that I lay down My life in order to take it up again"; John 17:24, addressed to the "Father", says "before the foundation of the world"; John 15:9 goes on "so have I loved you"; John 5:20 adds "shows Him all He does". Colossians 1:13 speaks of being brought "into the kingdom of His beloved Son".

rows.title: Put on the armor

The Law & history: The one putting on his armor should not boast like one taking it off
put a bronze helmet on his head, and dressed him in armor
Gospels & Acts: he takes away the armor in which the man trusted
The letters: Put on the full armor of God, so that you can make your stand against the devil's schemes
take up the full armor of God
lay aside the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light

rows.alike: Ephesians and Romans both tell the readers to "put on" armor: "the full armor of God" and "the armor of light".
rows.different: Ephesians 6:11 gives the reason "so that you can make your stand against the devil's schemes"; Romans 13:12 sets the armor against "the deeds of darkness". In Luke 11:22 armor is taken away: "the armor in which the man trusted". The asides speak of soldiers' armor.

rows.title: A belt around the waist

The Prophets: Righteousness will be the belt around His hips, and faithfulness the sash around His waist
The letters: with the belt of truth buckled around your waist

rows.alike: Both name a quality worn as a belt: "Righteousness will be the belt around His hips", "the belt of truth buckled around your waist".
rows.different: Isaiah 11:5 speaks of "His hips" and "His waist" and names "Righteousness" and "faithfulness"; Ephesians 6:14 is said to the readers ("your waist") and names "truth", giving righteousness to the breastplate instead.

rows.title: The breastplate of righteousness

The Law & history: the ephod itself, and the breastplate
The Prophets: He put on righteousness like a breastplate
The letters: with the breastplate of righteousness arrayed
putting on the breastplate of faith and love
Revelation: They also had breastplates like breastplates of iron

rows.alike: Isaiah 59:17 and Ephesians 6:14 join righteousness and the breastplate: "He put on righteousness like a breastplate", "the breastplate of righteousness". 1 Thessalonians 5:8 also speaks of "putting on the breastplate".
rows.different: In Isaiah 59:17 it is "He" who "put on righteousness like a breastplate", with "the helmet of salvation on His head"; Ephesians 6:14 ("your waist") and 1 Thessalonians 5:8 ("let us be sober, putting on the breastplate") are said to the readers. 1 Thessalonians 5:8 names "faith and love" for the breastplate, not righteousness. The asides are the breastplate Aaron is clothed with in Exodus 29:5 and the "breastplates of iron" of Revelation 9:9.

rows.title: Feet that bring the good news of peace

The Prophets: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of those who bring good news, who proclaim peace
the feet of one who brings good news, who proclaims peace!
The letters: As it is written: “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!
your feet fitted with the readiness of the gospel of peace

rows.alike: Each speaks of feet and good news: "the feet of those who bring good news", "your feet fitted with the readiness of the gospel of peace". Isaiah, Nahum and Ephesians add peace: "who proclaim peace", "who proclaims peace", "the gospel of peace".
rows.different: Isaiah 52:7 has the feet "on the mountains"; Nahum 1:15 says "Look to the mountains". Isaiah's messengers "proclaim salvation" and "say to Zion"; Nahum's verse goes on "Celebrate your feasts, O Judah". Romans 10:15 sets "As it is written" after "how can they preach unless they are sent?"; Ephesians 6:15 speaks of the readers' own feet, "fitted with the readiness".

rows.title: A shield

The Law & history: I am your shield, your very great reward
He is the shield that protects you, the sword in which you boast
Psalms & wisdom: You, O LORD, are a shield around me
The LORD is my strength and my shield
Take up Your shield and buckler
His faithfulness is a shield and rampart
He is a shield to those who take refuge in Him
The letters: take up the shield of faith

rows.alike: Each speaks of a shield, and two of taking one up: "Take up Your shield and buckler", "take up the shield of faith".
rows.different: In Genesis 15:1, Deuteronomy 33:29, Psalm 3:3 and Psalm 28:7 the shield is the LORD himself ("I am your shield", "He is the shield that protects you", "You, O LORD, are a shield around me", "The LORD is my strength and my shield"); Psalm 91:4 has "His faithfulness is a shield and rampart" and Proverbs 30:5 "He is a shield to those who take refuge in Him". Psalm 35:2 asks "Take up Your shield and buckler". In Ephesians 6:16 the readers are told to "take up the shield of faith".

rows.title: Flaming arrows

Psalms & wisdom: There He shattered the flaming arrows, the shield and sword and weapons of war
He ordains His arrows with fire
Like a madman shooting firebrands and deadly arrows
The letters: with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one

rows.alike: Psalm 76:3 and Ephesians 6:16 name "the flaming arrows", and Psalm 7:13 "His arrows with fire".
rows.different: In Psalm 76:3 "He shattered the flaming arrows" along with "the shield and sword and weapons of war"; in Psalm 7:13 the arrows are "His arrows", ordained "with fire". Ephesians 6:16 speaks of "the flaming arrows of the evil one", which "you can extinguish" with the shield of faith.

rows.title: The helmet of salvation

The Prophets: the helmet of salvation on His head
The letters: the helmet of our hope of salvation

rows.alike: Isaiah 59:17 and Ephesians 6:17 say "the helmet of salvation" in the same words; 1 Thessalonians 5:8 says "the helmet of our hope of salvation".
rows.different: Isaiah 59:17 has the helmet "on His head", with "garments of vengeance" and "a cloak of zeal", which Ephesians 6:17 and 1 Thessalonians 5:8 do not name. Ephesians 6:17 says "take the helmet of salvation"; 1 Thessalonians 5:8 says "putting on" it, and adds "our hope of".

rows.title: The word of God and the double-edged sword

The Law & history: Ehud had made for himself a double-edged sword a cubit long
Psalms & wisdom: May the high praises of God be in their mouths, and a double-edged sword in their hands
The letters: the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God
the word of God is living and active. Sharper than any double-edged sword
Revelation: a sharp double-edged sword came from His mouth
These are the words of the One who holds the sharp, double-edged sword

rows.alike: Ephesians 6:17 and Hebrews 4:12 set "the word of God" beside a sword: "the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God", "Sharper than any double-edged sword". Psalm 149:6 sets "the high praises of God" beside "a double-edged sword". Revelation 1:16 has "a sharp double-edged sword came from His mouth", and Revelation 2:12 has "the words of the One who holds the sharp, double-edged sword".
rows.different: Ephesians 6:17 calls "the sword of the Spirit" "the word of God"; Hebrews 4:12 says "the word of God is living and active. Sharper than any double-edged sword" and "It judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart". Psalm 149:6 puts "the high praises of God" "in their mouths" and "a double-edged sword in their hands". Proverbs 5:4 has "sharp as a double-edged sword" of "she", "in the end"; Judges 3:16 says "Ehud had made for himself a double-edged sword a cubit long".

rows.title: Watch and pray

The Law & history: So we prayed to our God and posted a guard against them day and night
Gospels & Acts: Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation
Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation
keep watch at all times, and pray
The letters: stay alert with all perseverance in your prayers for all the saints
Devote yourselves to prayer, being watchful and thankful
be clear-minded and sober, so that you can pray

rows.alike: Most join praying with keeping watch: "Watch and pray", "keep watch at all times, and pray", "stay alert with all perseverance in your prayers", "prayed to our God and posted a guard".
rows.different: Nehemiah 4:9 has "we prayed to our God and posted a guard against them day and night". Matthew and Mark add "so that you will not enter into temptation"; Luke 21:36 "that you may have the strength to escape all that is about to happen"; Ephesians 6:18 asks for prayers "for all the saints"; Colossians adds "thankful". 1 Peter 4:7 says "be clear-minded and sober, so that you can pray", and does not say watch.

rows.title: Be strong

The Law & history: David found strength in the LORD his God
Psalms & wisdom: Be strong and courageous, all you who hope in the LORD
You have armed me with strength for battle
The Prophets: be strong, all you people of the land
The letters: be strong in the Lord and in His mighty power
Be men of courage. Be strong.
be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus

rows.alike: "Be strong" is said in the Law and history, the Psalms, the Prophets and the letters, most often joined with courage: "be strong and courageous" (Deuteronomy 31:6, Joshua 1:9, Psalm 31:24 and others), "Be men of courage. Be strong." (1 Corinthians 16:13). Ephesians 6:10, 2 Timothy 2:1 and Haggai 2:4 say "be strong" without courage.
rows.different: Some say where the strength is: "in the Lord and in His mighty power" (Ephesians 6:10), "in the grace that is in Christ Jesus" (2 Timothy 2:1), "in the LORD his God" (1 Samuel 30:6). Many give a reason: "the LORD your God is with you wherever you go" (Joshua 1:9), "I will be with you" (Deuteronomy 31:23), "there is a greater One with us than with him" (2 Chronicles 32:7), "I am with you" (Haggai 2:4); Joshua 10:25 says "the LORD will do this to all the enemies you fight". Several add "Do not be afraid or discouraged" (Joshua 10:25, 1 Chronicles 22:13, 28:20, 2 Chronicles 32:7). Psalm 27:14 sets it beside "Wait patiently for the LORD" and Psalm 31:24 says it to "all you who hope in the LORD". Psalm 18:39 is said to one addressed as "You": "You have armed me with strength for battle".

rows.title: Stand firm

The Law & history: Stand firm and you will see the LORD's salvation
stand firm, and see the salvation of the LORD on your behalf
The Prophets: If you do not stand firm in your faith, then you will not stand at all
The letters: you will be able to stand your ground, and having done everything, to stand
you stand firm in one spirit

rows.alike: "Stand firm" in each column; Isaiah 7:9, 1 Corinthians 16:13 and 1 Peter 5:9 join it to faith: "stand firm in your faith", "Stand firm in the faith", "standing firm in your faith".
rows.different: In Exodus 14:13 and 2 Chronicles 20:17 those who stand firm will "see" the LORD's salvation, and 2 Chronicles says "You need not fight this battle". Isaiah 7:9 warns "then you will not stand at all". Ephesians 6:13 ties standing to "the full armor of God" and "the day of evil"; 1 Peter 5:9 says "Resist him, standing firm in your faith".

rows.title: Not according to the flesh: the weapons of the warfare

Psalms & wisdom: Wisdom is better than weapons of war
The Prophets: No weapon formed against you shall prosper
The letters: our struggle is not against flesh and blood
we do not wage war according to the flesh
The weapons of our warfare are not the weapons of the flesh. Instead, they have divine power to demolish strongholds
with the weapons of righteousness in the right hand and in the left

rows.alike: Weapons are set beside something other than themselves: "Wisdom is better than weapons of war", "No weapon formed against you shall prosper", "The weapons of our warfare are not the weapons of the flesh".
rows.different: Ecclesiastes and Isaiah speak of weapons of war and of weapons "formed against you"; 2 Corinthians speaks of "our" weapons, which "have divine power to demolish strongholds", and of "the weapons of righteousness". Ephesians 6:12 says whom the struggle is not against: "flesh and blood".

rows.title: Fight the good fight, fight the LORD's battles

The Law & history: Only be valiant for me and fight the LORD's battles
because he fights the LORD's battles
The letters: so that by them you may fight the good fight
Fight the good fight of the faith
I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith
like a good soldier of Christ Jesus

rows.alike: Each speaks of fighting and names it: "fight the LORD's battles", "Fight the good fight of the faith".
rows.different: 1 Samuel 18:17 is said to David, and sets Saul's thought beside it: "let the hand of the Philistines be against him"; 1 Samuel 25:28 says "because he fights the LORD's battles" of "my lord", in words that begin "Please forgive your servant's offense". In the letters it is "the good fight of the faith", charged to Timothy ("Timothy, my child") and said of himself by the writer: "I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith".

rows.title: The rulers and authorities in the heavenly realms

The letters: against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this world's darkness, and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms
made known to the rulers and authorities in the heavenly realms
far above all rule and authority, power and dominion
whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities. All things were created through Him and for Him
having disarmed the powers and authorities
with angels, authorities, and powers subject to Him

rows.alike: The letters name "rulers" and "authorities" together, with "powers", "dominions" and "principalities".
rows.different: Ephesians 6:12 names them as those "our struggle" is against, "in the heavenly realms"; Ephesians 3:10 says God's wisdom is "made known to" them; Colossians 1:16 says "All things were created through Him and for Him"; Colossians 2:15 says "having disarmed the powers and authorities"; 1 Peter 3:22 says "subject to Him". Luke 12:11 and Titus 3:1 use the words of the rulers before whom believers are brought and to whom they "submit".

rows.title: Resist the devil

The Prophets: the people who know their God will firmly resist him
Gospels & Acts: he left Him until an opportune time
The letters: Submit yourselves, then, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you
Resist him, standing firm in your faith
do not give the devil a foothold
make your stand against the devil's schemes
we are not unaware of his schemes

rows.alike: James and 1 Peter say "Resist the devil" and "Resist him"; James adds "he will flee from you".
rows.different: James sets "Submit yourselves, then, to God" before the command; 1 Peter adds "standing firm in your faith". Matthew 4:11 and Luke 4:13 say "the devil left Him"; Matthew goes on "and angels came and ministered to Him", Luke "until an opportune time"; neither verse says "resist". Ephesians and 2 Corinthians speak of "the devil's schemes" and "his schemes". Daniel 11:32 says "the people who know their God will firmly resist him", after "With flattery he will corrupt those who violate the covenant".

rows.title: Satan before the LORD, at the right hand to accuse

Psalms & wisdom: the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came with them
Satan also came with them to present himself before Him
let an accuser stand at his right hand
The Prophets: with Satan standing at his right hand to accuse him

rows.alike: Satan is named in Job and Zechariah: "Satan also came with them to present himself before Him", "with Satan standing at his right hand to accuse him". Psalm 109:6 and Zechariah 3:1 share "at his right hand" and an accuser: "let an accuser stand at his right hand".
rows.different: In Job 1:6 and 2:1 Satan comes "with" "the sons of God" "before the LORD"; in Zechariah 3:1 Satan stands "at his right hand" beside "Joshua the high priest", who is "standing before the angel of the LORD". Psalm 109:6 is worded "let an accuser stand at his right hand" and goes with "Set over him a wicked man".

rows.title: Incited, stirred up

The Law & history: Then Satan rose up against Israel and incited David to take a census of Israel
the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He stirred up David against them
Psalms & wisdom: even though you incited Me against him to ruin him without cause

rows.alike: Each says someone was incited or stirred up: "incited David to take a census of Israel", "He stirred up David against them", "you incited Me against him".
rows.different: The two accounts of David's census name different subjects: 2 Samuel 24:1 says "the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He stirred up David"; 1 Chronicles 21:1 says "Satan rose up against Israel and incited David". In Job 2:3 the LORD says to Satan "you incited Me against him".

rows.title: Rebuked

Gospels & Acts: He rebuked the demons and would not allow them to speak
rebuked Peter and said, “Get behind Me, Satan!
The letters: did not presume to bring a slanderous charge against him, but said, “The Lord rebuke you!

rows.alike: A rebuke in each: "The LORD rebukes you, Satan!", "The Lord rebuke you!", "Jesus rebuked the spirit".
rows.different: In Zechariah 3:2 the LORD speaks: "The LORD rebukes you, Satan!"; in Jude 1:9 "the archangel Michael" says "The Lord rebuke you!" to the devil and "did not presume to bring a slanderous charge against him". In the Gospels Jesus rebukes spirits and demons Himself, and in Mark 8:33 He rebukes Peter with "Get behind Me, Satan!".

rows.title: Unclean spirits commanded to come out

The Prophets: I will also remove the prophets and the spirit of impurity from the land
Gospels & Acts: He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey Him!
Come out of this man, you unclean spirit!
Jesus had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man
Jesus gave them authority over unclean spirits
giving them authority over unclean spirits
Lord, even the demons submit to us in Your name.
In the name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her!
I command you by Jesus, whom Paul proclaims.
Revelation: three unclean spirits that looked like frogs

rows.alike: "The spirit of impurity" is named in Zechariah 13:2, "three unclean spirits" in Revelation 16:13 and "unclean spirits" in the Gospels; in the Gospels and Acts spirits are commanded: "He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey Him!", "In the name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her!".
rows.different: Zechariah 13:2 says the LORD will "remove the prophets and the spirit of impurity from the land", with the names of the idols. Revelation 16:13 sees "three unclean spirits" coming "out of the mouths of the dragon, the beast, and the false prophet". Jesus gives "authority over unclean spirits" to the Twelve; Paul commands "In the name of Jesus Christ"; the itinerant Jewish exorcists of Acts 19 say "I command you by Jesus, whom Paul proclaims".

rows.title: The finger of God

The Law & history: This is the finger of God
tablets of stone inscribed by the finger of God
inscribed by the finger of God
Gospels & Acts: But if I drive out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you
But if I drive out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you

rows.alike: Exodus 8:19 and Luke 11:20 both speak of "the finger of God": "This is the finger of God", "if I drive out demons by the finger of God".
rows.different: In Exodus 8:19 "the magicians said to Pharaoh", and "Pharaoh's heart was hardened". Luke 11:20 has it of driving out demons, where Matthew 12:28 has "by the Spirit of God". The asides use the words of the stone tablets "inscribed by the finger of God".

rows.title: Michael

The Prophets: Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me
no one has the courage to support me against these, except Michael your prince
Michael, the great prince who stands watch over your people, will rise up
The letters: the archangel Michael, when he disputed with the devil over the body of Moses
Revelation: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon

rows.alike: Michael is named in each: "came to help me", "disputed with the devil", "fought against the dragon".
rows.different: Daniel calls him "one of the chief princes", "your prince" and "the great prince who stands watch over your people", and the one opposing is "the prince of the kingdom of Persia"; Jude calls him "the archangel" and names "the devil"; Revelation says "Michael and his angels" and names "the dragon".

rows.title: The prince of this world, the god of this age

Gospels & Acts: now the prince of this world will be cast out
the prince of this world is coming, and he has no claim on Me
the prince of this world has been condemned
The letters: The god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers
the ruler of the power of the air, the spirit who is now at work in the sons of disobedience
the whole world is under the power of the evil one

rows.alike: Each speaks of a power in "this world", "this age" or "the whole world": "the prince of this world", "The god of this age", "the ruler of the power of the air", "the whole world is under the power of the evil one".
rows.different: John's three verses use only "the prince of this world", and speak of the prince as "cast out", having "no claim on Me", and "condemned". Each letter has its own words: "The god of this age", who "has blinded the minds of unbelievers"; "the ruler of the power of the air", "now at work in the sons of disobedience"; "the evil one".

rows.title: Kept from the evil one

Psalms & wisdom: The LORD will guard you from all evil
Gospels & Acts: deliver us from the evil one
keep them from the evil one
The letters: He will strengthen you and guard you from the evil one
the One who was born of God protects him, and the evil one cannot touch him
the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one

rows.alike: Each asks, promises or provides keeping: "guard you from all evil", "guard you from the evil one", "keep them from the evil one", "deliver us from the evil one", "the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one" (Ephesians 6:16).
rows.different: Psalm 121:7 says "all evil"; the others say "the evil one". Matthew 6:13 asks "deliver us from the evil one"; John 17:15 says "I am not asking that You take them out of the world, but that You keep them from the evil one"; Psalm 121 and 2 Thessalonians promise; 1 John 5:18 says "the evil one cannot touch him"; Ephesians 6:16 speaks of "the shield of faith".

rows.title: The snare: escaped

Psalms & wisdom: Surely He will deliver you from the snare of the fowler
We have escaped like a bird from the snare of the fowler
The letters: so that he will not fall into disgrace and into the snare of the devil
escape the snare of the devil, who has taken them captive to his will

rows.alike: A snare, and escape from it: "We have escaped like a bird from the snare of the fowler", "escape the snare of the devil".
rows.different: The Psalms say "the snare of the fowler", and Psalm 91:3 that "He will deliver you"; the letters say "the snare of the devil", and 2 Timothy 2:26 adds "who has taken them captive to his will".

rows.title: Tempted

Gospels & Acts: Then Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil
He was there for forty days, being tempted by Satan
for forty days He was tempted by the devil
The letters: for fear that the tempter had somehow tempted you
so that Satan will not tempt you through your lack of self-control
He Himself suffered when He was tempted
one who was tempted in every way that we are, yet was without sin

rows.alike: Temptation is named in each, and in most a tempter: "to be tempted by the devil", "being tempted by Satan", "the tempter had somehow tempted you", "He Himself suffered when He was tempted".
rows.different: The Gospels tell of Jesus in the wilderness "for forty days". 1 Thessalonians 3:5 has "for fear that the tempter had somehow tempted you" and 1 Corinthians 7:5 "so that Satan will not tempt you". Hebrews 4:15 says "one who was tempted in every way that we are, yet was without sin", and Hebrews 2:18 and 4:15 name no tempter.

rows.title: Overcome

Gospels & Acts: take courage; I have overcome the world!
The letters: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good
you have overcome the evil one
have overcome them, because greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world
this is the victory that has overcome the world: our faith
you have overcome the evil one
Revelation: The one who overcomes will not be harmed by the second death
They have conquered him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony

rows.alike: Each speaks of overcoming: "I have overcome the world!", "you have overcome the evil one", "The one who overcomes", "They have conquered him".
rows.different: What is overcome differs: "the world" (John 16:33, 1 John 5:4), "evil" (Romans 12:21), "the evil one" (1 John 2:13, 2:14), "them" (1 John 4:4), "him" (Revelation 12:11). How differs too: "with good", "our faith", "because greater is He who is in you", "by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony", and in 1 John 2:14 "the word of God abides in you".

rows.title: Trodden under your feet

The Law & history: you shall trample their high places
Psalms & wisdom: You will tread on the lion and cobra; you will trample the young lion and serpent
The Prophets: you will trample the wicked, for they will be ashes under the soles of your feet
Gospels & Acts: I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy
The letters: The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet

rows.alike: Treading and trampling underfoot: "You will tread on the lion and cobra", "authority to tread on snakes and scorpions", "under the soles of your feet", "crush Satan under your feet".
rows.different: What is trodden differs: "their high places", "the lion and cobra ... the young lion and serpent", "the wicked", "snakes and scorpions, and ... all the power of the enemy", "Satan". In Romans 16:20 "The God of peace" does the crushing; in the others the hearers tread.

rows.title: Children of the devil

Gospels & Acts: You belong to your father, the devil
He was a murderer from the beginning
The weeds are the sons of the evil one
O child of the devil and enemy of all righteousness
The letters: the children of God are distinguished from the children of the devil
The one who practices sin is of the devil, because the devil has been sinning from the very start
Cain, who belonged to the evil one and murdered his brother

rows.alike: Some are called the devil's: "your father, the devil", "child of the devil", "the children of the devil", "the sons of the evil one", "belonged to the evil one". John 8:44 and 1 John 3:8 both say "from the beginning" or "from the very start".
rows.different: John 8:44 calls the devil "a murderer from the beginning" and "the father of lies"; Acts 13:10 says "O child of the devil and enemy of all righteousness"; Matthew 13:38 sets "The weeds are the sons of the evil one" beside "the good seed represents the sons of the kingdom"; 1 John 3:10 says how they are "distinguished", "Anyone who does not practice righteousness", and 3:12 names "Cain".

rows.title: The power of darkness

Gospels & Acts: this hour belongs to you and to the power of darkness
turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God
The letters: He has rescued us from the dominion of darkness
the powers of this world's darkness
lay aside the deeds of darkness
Have no fellowship with the fruitless deeds of darkness, but rather expose them

rows.alike: Darkness is named as a power or dominion: "the power of darkness", "the dominion of darkness", "the powers of this world's darkness"; Acts 26:18 sets "darkness" beside "the power of Satan".
rows.different: Luke 22:53 has "this hour belongs to you and to the power of darkness", after "you did not lay a hand on Me". Acts 26:18 and Colossians 1:13 speak of a turning or rescue, "from darkness to light", "into the kingdom of His beloved Son". Romans 13:12 and Ephesians 5:11 speak of "deeds of darkness" to lay aside or expose.

rows.title: Children of God

Gospels & Acts: He gave the right to become children of God
The letters: the glorious freedom of the children of God
it is not the children of the flesh who are God's children, but it is the children of the promise who are regarded as offspring
that we should be called children of God. And that is what we are!
we are now children of God
we love the children of God
the children of God are distinguished from the children of the devil

rows.alike: John and the letters use the same words, "children of God": "He gave the right to become children of God" (John 1:12), "we are now children of God" (1 John 3:2); Romans 8:16 has "we are God's children".
rows.different: In John 1:12 it is a right given "to all who did receive Him"; in 1 John 3:1 it is a name, "that we should be called children of God", and "that is what we are!"; Romans 9:8 sets "the children of the flesh" beside "the children of the promise"; John 11:52 speaks of "the scattered children of God", "to gather them together into one". 1 John 3:10 sets "the children of God" beside "the children of the devil".

rows.title: Sons of God; sons of the LORD your God

The Law & history: the sons of God had relations with the daughters of men
You are sons of the LORD your God
Psalms & wisdom: the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD
Gospels & Acts: since they are sons of the resurrection, they are sons of God
The letters: the revelation of the sons of God
You are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus

rows.alike: Each names some "sons of God", or in Deuteronomy "sons of the LORD your God"; Deuteronomy 14:1 and Galatians 3:26 both say it to their hearers: "You are sons", "You are all sons".
rows.different: In Genesis the sons of God are set beside "the daughters of men", and in Job they "came to present themselves before the LORD", "and Satan also came with them"; Luke 20:36 says those of the resurrection "are like the angels" and "are sons of God"; Galatians 3:26 adds "through faith in Christ Jesus", and Romans 8:19 speaks of "the revelation of the sons of God" that the creation waits for.

rows.title: Sons of the Most High; "You are gods"

Psalms & wisdom: You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High
Gospels & Acts: Is it not written in your Law
I have said you are gods
you will be sons of the Most High; for He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked
that you may be sons of your Father in heaven. He causes His sun to rise on the evil and the good

rows.alike: Psalm 82:6 and Luke 6:35 share the words "sons of the Most High", and Matthew 5:45 has "sons of your Father in heaven"; John 10:34 repeats the psalm's "I have said you are gods".
rows.different: The psalm states it, "You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High"; in Luke and Matthew it follows a command, "love your enemies", and the reason given is that "He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked" and sends His sun "on the evil and the good"; John cites the psalm as "written in your Law".

rows.title: Born of God

Gospels & Acts: children born not of blood, nor of the desire or will of man, but born of God
The letters: everyone who practices righteousness has been born of Him
Anyone born of God refuses to practice sin, because God's seed abides in him
Everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God
Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God
everyone born of God overcomes the world
anyone born of God does not keep on sinning

rows.alike: John's Gospel and 1 John use the same words, "born of God" (John 1:13; 1 John 3:9, 4:7, 5:1, 5:4).
rows.different: John 1:13 says what the birth is not: "not of blood, nor of the desire or will of man"; 1 John says what goes with it: one who "practices righteousness", "loves", "believes that Jesus is the Christ", "overcomes the world", and "refuses to practice sin".

rows.title: Born again; the God who gave you birth

The Law & history: you forgot the God who gave you birth
Gospels & Acts: no one can see the kingdom of God unless he is born again
The letters: through the washing of new birth and renewal by the Holy Spirit
He chose to give us birth through the word of truth
He has given us new birth into a living hope
you have been born again, not of perishable seed, but of imperishable, through the living and enduring word of God

rows.alike: God is the one who gives birth: "the God who gave you birth" (Deuteronomy 32:18), "He chose to give us birth" (James 1:18), "He has given us new birth" (1 Peter 1:3); John 3:3 and 1 Peter 1:23 share "born again".
rows.different: Deuteronomy says "you forgot the God who gave you birth"; in John it is a condition, "unless he is born again"; James and 1 Peter name the means as "the word of truth" and "the living and enduring word of God", 1 Peter 1:3 "the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead", and Titus 3:5 "the washing of new birth and renewal by the Holy Spirit".

rows.title: Heirs

The Law & history: a servant in my household will be my heir
one who comes from your own body will be your heir
The Prophets: heirs from Judah; My elect will possess My mountains
The letters: the promise to Abraham and his offspring that he would be heir of the world
if those who live by the law are heirs, faith is useless
if we are children, then we are heirs: heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ
you are Abraham's seed and heirs according to the promise
as long as the heir is a child, he is no different from a slave
we would become heirs with the hope of eternal life
His Son, whom He appointed heir of all things
became heir of the righteousness that comes by faith
Isaac and Jacob, who were heirs with him of the same promise
fellow heirs of the gracious gift of life

rows.alike: The word is "heir" throughout, and several tie it to Abraham and a promise: "your heir" (Genesis 15:4), "heir of the world" (Romans 4:13), "heirs according to the promise" (Galatians 3:29), "heirs of the promise" (Hebrews 6:17).
rows.different: Genesis 15:4 says "one who comes from your own body"; Isaiah 65:9 "heirs from Judah"; Romans 8:17 joins heirs to children, "if we are children, then we are heirs"; Ephesians 3:6 says "the Gentiles are fellow heirs"; Hebrews 1:2 speaks of "His Son, whom He appointed heir of all things"; and what is inherited differs: "the world", "eternal life", "the gracious gift of life", "all things".

rows.title: Abba, Father

Gospels & Acts: all things are possible for You. Take this cup from Me. Yet not what I will, but what You will.
The letters: God sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying out, “Abba, Father!”

rows.alike: Both have the same two words, "Abba, Father".
rows.different: In Mark 14:36 the words come with "Take this cup from Me"; in Galatians 4:6 it is "the Spirit of His Son" in "our hearts" that is "crying out", "because you are sons".

rows.title: You are our Father; call Me ‘Father'

The Law & history: Is He not your Father and Creator?
The Prophets: O LORD, You are our Father; we are the clay, and You are the potter
Have you not just called to Me, ‘My Father, You are my friend from youth.
I thought you would call Me ‘Father' and never turn away from following Me
A son honors his father, and a servant his master. But if I am a father, where is My honor?
Gospels & Acts: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name
The letters: Since you call on a Father who judges each one's work impartially

rows.alike: God is named or called on as Father: "You are our Father" (Isaiah 64:8), "call Me 'Father'" (Jeremiah 3:19), "Our Father in heaven" (Matthew 6:9), "you call on a Father" (1 Peter 1:17).
rows.different: In Deuteronomy, Jeremiah and Malachi it comes with a question or a lament against those spoken to: "Is this how you repay the LORD", "never turn away from following Me", and, to "you priests", "where is My honor?"; in Isaiah it is the people's own plea, "we are the clay"; in Matthew and Luke it is how to pray; 1 Peter adds that this Father "judges each one's work impartially".

rows.title: He will be My son, and I will be his Father

The Law & history: He will be My son, and I will be his Father
for I have chosen him as My son, and I will be his Father
Psalms & wisdom: He will call to Me, ‘You are my Father, my God, the Rock of my salvation.'

rows.alike: God speaks of a son and of Himself as his Father: "He will be My son, and I will be his Father" (1 Chronicles 22:10), "I have chosen him as My son, and I will be his Father" (1 Chronicles 28:6); Psalm 89:26 has "He will call to Me, 'You are my Father, my God, the Rock of my salvation.'"
rows.different: 1 Chronicles 28:6 names him, "Solomon your son", and 22:10 ties it to the house: "the one who will build a house for My Name"; Psalm 89:26 names no one in the verse, and has the words "You are my Father, my God, the Rock of my salvation."

rows.title: My sons and My daughters

The Law & history: provoked to anger by His sons and daughters
The Prophets: Bring My sons from afar, and My daughters from the ends of the earth

rows.alike: Both speak of the LORD's sons and daughters: "His sons and daughters" (Deuteronomy 32:19), "My sons from afar, and My daughters from the ends of the earth" (Isaiah 43:6).
rows.different: In Deuteronomy the LORD "rejected them, provoked to anger by His sons and daughters"; in Isaiah He calls for them to be brought "from afar" and "from the ends of the earth".

rows.title: My son; My firstborn

The Law & history: let My son go so that he may worship Me
The Prophets: For I am Israel's Father, and Ephraim is My firstborn

rows.alike: The speaker says "My son" and "My firstborn": "let My son go so that he may worship Me" (Exodus 4:23), "Ephraim is My firstborn" (Jeremiah 31:9).
rows.different: Exodus 4:23 ends with a threat, "I will kill your firstborn son!"; Jeremiah 31:9 is a promise to those who "come with weeping", and adds "I am Israel's Father".

rows.title: Discipline your son; the rod

The Law & history: When he does wrong, I will discipline him with the rod of men
Psalms & wisdom: If his sons forsake My law
I will attend to their transgression with the rod
He who spares the rod hates his son, but he who loves him disciplines him diligently
Discipline your son, for in that there is hope
the rod of discipline drives it far from him
Do not withhold discipline from a child
Discipline your son, and he will give you rest
The letters: If you do not experience discipline like everyone else, then you are illegitimate children and not true sons
we have all had earthly fathers who disciplined us, and we respected them. Should we not much more submit to the Father of our spirits and live?
Our fathers disciplined us for a short time as they thought best, but God disciplines us for our good

rows.alike: A son is disciplined, often "with the rod": "I will discipline him with the rod of men" (2 Samuel 7:14), "He who spares the rod hates his son" (Proverbs 13:24), "earthly fathers who disciplined us" (Hebrews 12:9).
rows.different: In 2 Samuel and Psalm 89 it is God who will discipline, "him" and "his sons"; Proverbs speaks to a father, "Discipline your son", and does not name God; Hebrews sets "earthly fathers" beside "the Father of our spirits" and says lack of discipline means "not true sons".

rows.title: A father of the fatherless

The Law & history: He executes justice for the fatherless and widow
Psalms & wisdom: You are the helper of the fatherless
to vindicate the fatherless and oppressed
A father of the fatherless and a defender of widows is God in His holy habitation
He sustains the fatherless and the widow
The Prophets: in You the fatherless find compassion
Abandon your orphans; I will preserve their lives
Gospels & Acts: I will not leave you as orphans; I will come to you

rows.alike: The fatherless are named with God as the one who acts for them: "A father of the fatherless" (Psalm 68:5), "the helper of the fatherless" (Psalm 10:14), "He sustains the fatherless" (Psalm 146:9); several add "the widow".
rows.different: Only Psalm 68:5 calls God "A father" of them; Hosea 14:3 has "in You the fatherless find compassion"; Jeremiah 49:11 has "Abandon your orphans; I will preserve their lives"; John 14:18 has "I will not leave you as orphans; I will come to you".

rows.title: Rebellious children; a perverse and crooked generation

The Law & history: the blemish on them is not that of His children, but of a perverse and crooked generation
they are a perverse generation-children of unfaithfulness
The Prophets: I have raised children and brought them up, but they have rebelled against Me
deceitful children, children unwilling to obey the LORD's instruction
They are surely My people, sons who will not be disloyal
They are foolish children, without understanding
But the children rebelled against Me
The letters: children of God without fault in a crooked and perverse generation

rows.alike: The word "children" is used of those who turn from God: "they have rebelled against Me" (Isaiah 1:2), "rebellious children" (Isaiah 30:1), "faithless children" (Jeremiah 3:14); and Deuteronomy 32:5 and Philippians 2:15 share the words "perverse and crooked generation" / "crooked and perverse generation".
rows.different: Deuteronomy 32:5 says the blemish "is not that of His children"; Isaiah 63:8 has God saying "sons who will not be disloyal"; Jeremiah calls them to "Return"; in Philippians 2:15 the generation is the one in which the hearers are to be "children of God without fault".

rows.title: Children of God and children of the devil

Gospels & Acts: Our only Father is God Himself
If God were your Father, you would love Me
You belong to your father, the devil
the good seed represents the sons of the kingdom. The weeds are the sons of the evil one
O child of the devil and enemy of all righteousness
The letters: By this the children of God are distinguished from the children of the devil

rows.alike: Each speaks of being the child of God or of the devil, the evil one: "You are doing the works of your father" (John 8:41), "the sons of the evil one" (Matthew 13:38), "child of the devil" (Acts 13:10), "the children of God are distinguished from the children of the devil" (1 John 3:10).
rows.different: In John 8 the hearers say "Our only Father is God Himself" and Jesus answers "If God were your Father, you would love Me"; Matthew 13:38 is the explanation of a parable, "the good seed" and "The weeds"; Acts 13:10 is said to one man; 1 John 3:10 gives the test: "Anyone who does not practice righteousness is not of God".

rows.title: Sons of light, children of light

Gospels & Acts: the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the sons of light
believe in the Light, so that you may become sons of light
The letters: you are all sons of the light and sons of the day

rows.alike: The same wording: "sons of light" (Luke 16:8, John 12:36), "sons of the light" (1 Thessalonians 5:5) and "children of light" (Ephesians 5:8).
rows.different: John 12:36 says how to "become sons of light": "believe in the Light"; Ephesians 5:8 says "you were once darkness"; Luke 16:8 sets them beside "the sons of this age"; 1 Thessalonians 5:5 adds "sons of the day".

rows.title: Carried, as a man carries his son

The Law & history: how I carried you on eagles' wings and brought you to Myself
the LORD your God carried you, as a man carries his son
The Prophets: who have been sustained from the womb, carried along since birth
I have made you, and I will carry you
He lifted them up and carried them all the days of old

rows.alike: The LORD "carried" His people: "carried you" (Exodus 19:4; Deuteronomy 1:31), "carried along since birth" (Isaiah 46:3), "carried them all the days of old" (Isaiah 63:9).
rows.different: Deuteronomy 1:31 gives the likeness "as a man carries his son", and Exodus 19:4 "on eagles' wings"; Deuteronomy speaks of "the wilderness", Isaiah 46 of "from the womb" and "to your old age".

rows.title: Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom; walk in freedom, live in freedom

Psalms & wisdom: And I will walk in freedom, for I have sought Your precepts.
The letters: where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
Be careful, however, that your freedom does not become a stumbling block to the weak.
For why should my freedom be determined by someone else's conscience?
to spy on our freedom in Christ Jesus, in order to enslave us.
For you, brothers, were called to freedom; but do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh.
Speak and act as those who are going to be judged by the law that gives freedom.
Live in freedom, but do not use your freedom as a cover-up for evil; live as servants of God.

rows.alike: Most speak of freedom as something to walk or live in, or to guard: 'I will walk in freedom' (Psalm 119:45), 'Live in freedom' (1 Peter 2:16), 'called to freedom' (Galatians 5:13), 'our freedom in Christ Jesus' (Galatians 2:4).
rows.different: Psalm 119:45 joins it to 'for I have sought Your precepts'; 2 Corinthians 3:17 says 'where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom'; Galatians 2:4 speaks of those who 'spy on our freedom in Christ Jesus, in order to enslave us'; 1 Corinthians 10:29 asks 'why should my freedom be determined by someone else's conscience?'; and Galatians 5:13, 1 Peter 2:16 and 1 Corinthians 8:9 each add a caution: 'do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh', 'do not use your freedom as a cover-up for evil', 'that your freedom does not become a stumbling block to the weak'. James 2:12 speaks of 'the law that gives freedom'.

rows.title: Be strong and courageous; do not be afraid or discouraged

The Law & history: Do not be afraid or discouraged.
Be strong and courageous; do not be afraid or terrified of them
Be strong and courageous, for you will go with this people into the land
Do not be afraid or discouraged.
Be strong and courageous, for you will bring the Israelites into the land
Have I not commanded you to be strong and courageous?
Above all, be strong and courageous!
Do not be afraid or discouraged.
Be strong and courageous, for the LORD will do this to all the enemies you fight.
be strong and courageous, for though Saul your lord is dead
Do not be afraid. Have I not commanded you? Be courageous and valiant!
Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or discouraged.
Be strong and courageous, and do it. Do not be afraid or discouraged
Do not be afraid or discouraged because of this vast army
Do not be afraid or discouraged.
Be strong and courageous! Do not be afraid or discouraged before the king of Assyria
Psalms & wisdom: Wait patiently for the LORD; be strong and courageous.
Be strong and courageous, all you who hope in the LORD.
The Prophets: Do not be afraid or disheartened
Be strong now; be very strong!
But now be strong, O Zerubbabel
Do not be afraid; let your hands be strong.

rows.alike: Each tells someone to be strong or not to be afraid: 'Be strong and courageous', 'Do not be afraid or discouraged', 'Be strong, do not fear!' (Isaiah 35:4). Many give a reason with 'for': 'for the LORD will do this to all the enemies you fight' (Joshua 10:25, in Joshua's words), 'for there is a greater One with us than with him' (2 Chronicles 32:7).
rows.different: The speakers differ: the LORD to Joshua (Joshua 8:1; Deuteronomy 31:23), Moses to Joshua (Deuteronomy 31:7), David to Solomon (1 Chronicles 28:20), 'the LORD says' to 'all you people of Judah and Jerusalem' (2 Chronicles 20:15), Psalm 31:24 to 'all you who hope in the LORD', and Absalom to the young men he has ordered to strike Amnon down: 'Do not be afraid. Have I not commanded you? Be courageous and valiant!' (2 Samuel 13:28). Isaiah 35:4 goes on 'Behold, your God will come with vengeance'.

rows.title: Take courage

The Law & history: Take courage and be men, O Philistines!
Gospels & Acts: Take courage, son; your sins are forgiven.
Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.
Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.
But take courage; I have overcome the world!
Take courage! As you have testified about Me in Jerusalem, so also you must testify in Rome.
keep up your courage, because you will not experience any loss of life
So take courage, men, for I believe God that it will happen just as He told me.
The letters: Be men of courage. Be strong.

rows.alike: Each says 'Take courage' or close to it ('Be men of courage' in 1 Corinthians 16:13), and many give a reason with it: 'your sins are forgiven', said to the paralytic (Matthew 9:2), 'It is I' (Matthew 14:27), 'I have overcome the world' (John 16:33), 'for I believe God' (Acts 27:25).
rows.different: Jesus says it in Matthew 9:2, 9:22, 14:27 and Mark 6:50, and in Acts 23:11 'the Lord stood near Paul' and said it. John 16:33 sets it after 'In the world you will have tribulation'. In Mark 10:49 'they' who called the blind man say 'Take courage!' and 'He is calling for you'; Acts 27:22 speaks of 'loss of life, but only of the ship' and 27:25 says 'take courage, men'; in 1 Samuel 4:9 it is said to the Philistines, 'Otherwise, you will serve the Hebrews'. 1 Corinthians 16:13 has 'Be men of courage', as 1 Samuel 4:9 has 'be men'.

rows.title: Do not be afraid: your prayer has been heard

The Law & history: Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he lies.
The Prophets: your words were heard, and I have come in response to them.
Gospels & Acts: Do not be afraid, Zechariah, because your prayer has been heard.
Cornelius stared at him in fear
Cornelius, your prayer has been heard

rows.alike: Each tells someone not to be afraid, or comes to one who is afraid, and gives as the reason that a voice or a prayer has been heard: 'God has heard the voice of the boy' (Genesis 21:17), 'your words were heard' (Daniel 10:12), 'your prayer has been heard' (Luke 1:13, Acts 10:31).
rows.different: What is heard differs, and each is said to one person: in Genesis 21:17, said to Hagar, 'the voice of the boy'; in Daniel 10:12, to Daniel, his words 'from the first day that you purposed to understand'; in Luke 1:13 to Zechariah and Acts 10:31 to Cornelius, a prayer. Luke adds 'Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son', and Acts 10:31 'your gifts to the poor have been remembered before God'.

rows.title: Touched, and told 'Do not be afraid'

The Prophets: Then he touched me, helped me to my feet
Do not be afraid, you who are highly precious
Gospels & Acts: Then Jesus came over and touched them.
Revelation: But He placed His right hand on me
Do not be afraid. I am the First and the Last

rows.alike: In each there is a touch and a person on the ground or shaking: 'my face to the ground' and 'he touched me' (Daniel 8:18), 'a hand touched me and set me trembling on my hands and knees' (Daniel 10:10), 'fell facedown in terror' and 'Jesus came over and touched them' (Matthew 17:6-7), 'fell at His feet like a dead man' and 'He placed His right hand on me' (Revelation 1:17). In Daniel 10, Matthew and Revelation the words that follow are 'Do not be afraid'.
rows.different: Daniel 8:18 has no 'Do not be afraid'; Daniel 10:19 adds 'Peace be with you! Be strong now', Matthew 'Get up', and Revelation 'I am the First and the Last'. The one who touches is 'the one with the likeness of a man' in Daniel 10:18 and 'Jesus' in Matthew 17:7.

rows.title: The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?

Psalms & wisdom: in God I trust. I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
The LORD is on my side; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
The Prophets: I will strengthen you; I will surely help you
Do not fear, I will help you.
Do not fear, O Jacob, you worm, O few men of Israel. I will help you
Do not fear the scorn of men
Why should you be afraid of mortal man
Gospels & Acts: Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul.
do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do no more.
The letters: The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?

rows.alike: Each speaks of not fearing, and many set it against people: 'I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?' (Psalm 56:4, Psalm 118:6, Hebrews 13:6), 'Do not fear the scorn of men' (Isaiah 51:7), 'Do not be afraid of those who kill the body' (Matthew 10:28, Luke 12:4). Isaiah 41:13 says 'Do not fear, I will help you.'
rows.different: In Psalms 56 and 118 the speaker says it of himself, and in Hebrews 13:6 'we say' it; in Isaiah 41 the LORD says to Jacob, 'I will help you'; Luke 12:4 says it to 'My friends', and Matthew 10:28 goes on 'Instead, fear the One who can destroy both soul and body in hell'. Hebrews 13:6 has 'The Lord is my helper' where Psalm 118:6 has 'The LORD is on my side'.

rows.title: Do not fear what they fear

The Prophets: Do not fear what they fear; do not live in dread.
The letters: Do not fear what they fear; do not be shaken.
Revelation: Do not fear what you are about to suffer

rows.alike: Isaiah 8:12 and 1 Peter 3:14 both say 'Do not fear what they fear'; Revelation 2:10 says 'Do not fear what you are about to suffer'.
rows.different: Isaiah 8:12 begins 'Do not call conspiracy everything these people regard as conspiracy' and ends 'do not live in dread'; 1 Peter 3:14 says first 'even if you should suffer for what is right, you are blessed' and ends 'do not be shaken'. Revelation 2:10 goes on 'the devil is about to throw some of you into prison to test you, and you will suffer tribulation for ten days'.

rows.title: Even the hairs of your head

The Law & history: not a hair of his head will fall to the ground
not a hair of your son's head will fall to the ground.
not a single hair of his will fall to the ground.
Gospels & Acts: Yet not one of them will fall to the ground apart from the will of your Father.
And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered.
So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
Yet not one of them is forgotten by God.
And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
Yet not even a hair of your head will perish.
not a single hair of your head will be lost.
you cannot make a single hair white or black

rows.alike: Each speaks of a hair, or a sparrow, kept or counted: 'not a hair of his head will fall to the ground' (1 Samuel 14:45), 'not one of them will fall to the ground apart from the will of your Father' (Matthew 10:29), 'not even a hair of your head will perish' (Luke 21:18).
rows.different: In 1 Samuel 14:45 the people say it to Saul of Jonathan ('As surely as the LORD lives'); in 2 Samuel 14:11 it is a vow, 'not a hair of your son's head will fall to the ground'; in 1 Kings 1:52 Solomon says it on a condition, 'If he is a man of character'. Only Matthew 10:30-31 and Luke 12:7 join it to 'So do not be afraid' and to 'the very hairs of your head are all numbered'. Acts 27:34 gives it as a reason to 'eat something': 'not a single hair of your head will be lost'. Matthew 5:36 uses 'a single hair' of swearing by one's head: 'you cannot make a single hair white or black'.

rows.title: Lie down with nothing to fear; no one to frighten them

The Law & history: you will lie down with nothing to fear
Psalms & wisdom: You will lie down without fear
When you lie down, you will not be afraid; when you rest, your sleep will be sweet.
I will lie down and sleep in peace, for You alone, O LORD, make me dwell in safety
The Prophets: they will be left to the flocks, which will lie down with no one to fear.
Jacob will return to quiet and ease, with no one to make him afraid.
Jacob will return to quiet and ease, with no one to make him afraid.
They will dwell securely, and no one will frighten them.
when they dwell securely in their land, with no one to frighten them.
each man will sit under his own vine and under his own fig tree, with no one to frighten him.
with nothing to frighten them away
But they will feed and lie down, with no one to make them tremble.
the needy will lie down in safety

rows.alike: Each speaks of lying down, or dwelling, safe, most with no fear: 'you will lie down with nothing to fear' (Leviticus 26:6), 'You will lie down without fear' (Job 11:19), 'with no one to frighten him' (Micah 4:4), 'with no one to make him afraid' (Jeremiah 30:10).
rows.different: Leviticus 26:6 sets it beside 'I will give peace to the land'; Job 11:19 goes on 'and many will court your favor'; Proverbs 3:24 adds 'your sleep will be sweet'. Jeremiah 30:10 and 46:27 say it to 'Jacob My servant' and 'O Israel', Zephaniah 3:13 of 'The remnant of Israel', and Ezekiel 39:26 'in their land'; Micah 4:4 has 'each man will sit under his own vine and under his own fig tree'. Psalm 4:8 says 'I will lie down and sleep in peace', and Isaiah 14:30 says of 'the needy' that they 'will lie down in safety'. Isaiah 17:2 uses the words of flocks in forsaken cities, and Nahum 2:11 of lions.

rows.title: Not a spirit of fear

The Prophets: for you will have no fear. Terror will be far removed
The letters: you did not receive a spirit of slavery that returns you to fear
For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
and free those who all their lives were held in slavery by their fear of death.
There is no fear in love, but perfect love drives out fear

rows.alike: Each speaks of fear taken away or not given: 'you will have no fear' (Isaiah 54:14), 'God has not given us a spirit of fear' (2 Timothy 1:7), 'perfect love drives out fear' (1 John 4:18).
